+waits doubling from 0.1 s to 1 s, the desk's Retry-After honoured up to that maximum, `max_retries=0` meaning no retry,
+and the same rule as the load driver. A fake clock makes every check exact (sleeping moves the clock; nothing waits)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import http.client
+import threading
+import time
+from email.utils import formatdate
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+from support import FakeClock
+
+from demo_only import burst
+from lead_desk.constants import (
+    BURST_BACKOFF_MAX_SECONDS,
+    BURST_BACKOFF_SECONDS,
+    BURST_RETRY_DEADLINE_SECONDS,
+    HTTP_BUSY,
+    HTTP_CREATED,
+)
+from load_tools import load_driver
+
+HTTP_NOT_FOUND = 404
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def clock(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> FakeClock:
+    return FakeClock(monkeypatch)
+
+
+MAX_CALLS = 5000  # the longest honest loop here makes about 300 tries
+
+
+def always(res: int | str, retry_after: float | None = None) -> Any:
+    calls: list[float] = []
+
+    def post() -> tuple[int | str, float | None, Any]:
+        assert len(calls) < MAX_CALLS, "the loop under test never ends"
+        calls.append(time.monotonic())
+        return res, retry_after, {"n": len(calls)}
+
+    post.calls = calls  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    return post
+
+
+def test_a_busy_desk_is_retried_for_the_whole_deadline_not_for_a_count(clock: FakeClock) -> None:
+    """Fails on a count loop (6 tries, about 0.5 s): by time the loop keeps going until 30 s have passed."""
+    post = always(HTTP_BUSY)
+    res, reply = burst.post_with_retries(post)
+    assert res == HTTP_BUSY and reply == {"n": len(post.calls)}
+    assert len(post.calls) > 25  # 0.1 + 0.2 + 0.4 + 0.8, then 1 s waits: about 33 tries in 30 s
+    assert post.calls[-1] - post.calls[0] <= BURST_RETRY_DEADLINE_SECONDS  # no try starts after the deadline
+    assert clock.now - post.calls[0] == pytest.approx(BURST_RETRY_DEADLINE_SECONDS)  # the last wait is cut to fit
+
+
+def test_waits_double_and_stop_growing_at_the_maximum(clock: FakeClock) -> None:
+    burst.post_with_retries(always("refused"), deadline=5.0)
+    assert clock.sleeps[:5] == pytest.approx([0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8, BURST_BACKOFF_MAX_SECONDS])
+    assert max(clock.sleeps) <= BURST_BACKOFF_MAX_SECONDS
+
+
+def test_the_desks_retry_after_is_honoured_up_to_the_maximum(clock: FakeClock) -> None:
+    burst.post_with_retries(always(HTTP_BUSY, retry_after=1.0), deadline=3.5)
+    assert clock.sleeps[:3] == pytest.approx([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])  # not 0.1, 0.2, 0.4: the desk asked for a second

+    burst.post_with_retries(always(HTTP_BUSY, retry_after=60.0), deadline=10.0)
+    assert max(clock.sleeps) == pytest.approx(BURST_BACKOFF_MAX_SECONDS)  # capped at the back-off maximum

body:
Method doesn't use the class instance and could be converted into a static method


The method doesn't use its bound instance. Decorate this method with `@staticmethod` decorator, so that Python does not have to instantiate a bound method for every instance of this class thereby saving memory and computation. Read more about staticmethods [here](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#staticmethod).

+

+    never decides its result by chance. Only the 6-byte token of a lead number is changed."""

+    def forced(nbytes: int | None = None) -> str:
+        if nbytes != 6:  # LEAD_ID_HEX_CHARS // 2: the lead number

+

+NUDGE_TO_TEST: Final = "reminder@example.test"  # the one reminder address of the tests

+    "name": "Ada Example",
+    "email": "Ada@Example.test",
+    "phone": "555 0100",
+    "company": "Example Ltd",
+    "message": "Please call me.",
+}
+
+

+    return {k: v for k, v in d.items() if v is not None}
+
+

+    """Environment for a child process: PYTHONPATH = src and the repo root (pytest's pythonpath is not inherited)."""
+    env = dict(os.environ)
+    env["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join([str(REPO / "src"), str(REPO)])
+    env.update(extra)
+    return env
+
+

+        s.bind((HOST, 0))
+        return int(s.getsockname()[1])
+
+

+    """Run one statement on the lead book through a separate connection and commit (a test's own write)."""
+    con = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=10)
+    try:
+        con.execute(sql, args)
+        con.commit()
+    finally:
+        con.close()
+
+
+def sql(rig: Rig, text: str, args: tuple[Any, ...] = ()) -> None:
+    sql_exec(rig.db_path, text, args)
+
+

+    """Make closing `sock` send a reset (SO_LINGER on, zero seconds) instead of a normal close."""
+    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0))
+

+def wait_until(fn: Callable[[], Any], timeout: float = WAIT_SECONDS, what: str = "condition") -> Any:

+    while True:
+        try:
+            val = fn()
+        except (OSError, ValueError):
+            val = None

+        if time.monotonic() > end:

+class Clock:
+    def __init__(self, start: int = 1_700_000_000) -> None:
+        self.t = start
+
+    def __call__(self) -> int:
+        return self.t
+
+    def advance(self, seconds: int) -> None:
+        self.t += seconds

+MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS = 5000  # a loop on the fake clock that sleeps more often than this is stuck
+MIN_FAKE_STEP = 1e-6  # seconds a fake sleep always advances the clock
+
+
+class FakeClock:
+    """time.monotonic and time.sleep for the module under test: sleeping moves the clock, nothing really waits."""
+
+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:  # a pytest MonkeyPatch
+        self.now = 1000.0
+        self.sleeps: list[float] = []
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "monotonic", lambda: self.now)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", self._sleep)

+    def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:

+        assert len(self.sleeps) < MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS, "the loop under test never ends"

+    passed the row's wait, so a frozen Clock would leave every row the request's own drive gave back for ever."""
+

+        super().__init__(int(time.time()))  # wall-clock: the desk's own calendar stamps
+
+    def __call__(self) -> int:
+        return int(time.time())  # wall-clock: the desk's own calendar stamps
+
+

+    as a kill would."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *points: str) -> None:
+        self.points = set(points)
+        self.fired: list[str] = []
+
+    def crash_point(self, name: str, conn: sqlite3.Connection | None) -> None:
+        if name in self.points and name not in self.fired:
+            self.fired.append(name)
+            if conn is not None and conn.in_transaction:
+                conn.rollback()
+            raise SimulatedCrash(name)
+
+
+class BlockAt(Hooks):
+    """Block once at `point` until release is set (holds a receipt open, or a follow-up in `sending`)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, point: str) -> None:
+        self.point = point
+        self.reached = threading.Event()
+        self.release = threading.Event()
+        self._used = False
+
+    def crash_point(self, name: str, conn: sqlite3.Connection | None) -> None:
+        if name == self.point and not self._used:
+            self._used = True
+            self.reached.set()
+            self.release.wait(timeout=WAIT_SECONDS)
+
+
+class CountingCrm:
+    """An in-process CRM that tells a double put apart from a harmless repeat. capability "keyed": a second put with
+    the same lead id is ALREADY_PRESENT and stores nothing. "blind": it cannot tell, so EVERY put stores one more
+    row. `calls` is the log of every put (lead id, record); `rows` the stored ones, so a double put on either kind
+    shows as len(rows) == 2 (blind) or len(calls) > the allowed number (keyed)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mode: str = "keyed") -> None:
+        if mode not in ("keyed", "blind"):
+            raise ValueError(mode)
+        self.capability = mode
+        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        self.rows: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        # every set_fields call (lead id, email key, CRM owner id, CRM status); kept apart from `calls` because tests
+        # assert on the number of puts there
+        self.set_fields_calls: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    @property
+    def count(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.rows)
+
+    def put(self, lead_id: str, record: Any) -> str:
+        with self._lock:
+            self.calls.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            if self.capability == "keyed" and any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                return "ALREADY_PRESENT"
+            self.rows.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            return "PUT"
+
+    def set_fields(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str, crm_owner_id: str, crm_status: str) -> None:
+        """Logs into set_fields_calls only; a lead with no stored put has no contact (as FakeCrm and HubSpot)."""
+        with self._lock:
+            self.set_fields_calls.append((lead_id, email_key, crm_owner_id, crm_status))
+            if not any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                raise CrmNothingStored("no contact")
+
+
+# -- desk builder
+@dataclass
+class Rig:
+    desk: Desk
+    config: Config
+    crm: Any
+    outbox: Any
+    qualifier: RecordedQualifier
+    clock: Clock
+    db_path: Path
+    replies_path: Path
+    desks: list[Desk] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def query(self, sql: str, args: tuple[Any, ...] = ()) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:
+        return rows(self.db_path, sql, args)
+
+    def leads(self) -> int:
+        return int(self.query("SELECT count(*) FROM leads")[0][0])
+
+    def state(self, lead_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+        sql = "SELECT state, last_error FROM followups" + (" WHERE lead_id=?" if lead_id else "")  # noqa: S608

Possible SQL injection vector through string-based query construction.


Constructing SQL query using user provided data is insecure. It makes application vulnerable to [SQL injection]([SQL injection](https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/SQL_Injection)) attacks.

+class CrashAt(Hooks):
+    """Raise SimulatedCrash once at each named point (one-shot per point). An open transaction is rolled back first,
+    as a kill would."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *points: str) -> None:
+        self.points = set(points)
+        self.fired: list[str] = []
+
+    def crash_point(self, name: str, conn: sqlite3.Connection | None) -> None:
+        if name in self.points and name not in self.fired:
+            self.fired.append(name)
+            if conn is not None and conn.in_transaction:
+                conn.rollback()
+            raise SimulatedCrash(name)
+
+
+class BlockAt(Hooks):
+    """Block once at `point` until release is set (holds a receipt open, or a follow-up in `sending`)."""
+

+        self.point = point
+        self.reached = threading.Event()
+        self.release = threading.Event()
+        self._used = False
+
+    def crash_point(self, name: str, conn: sqlite3.Connection | None) -> None:
+        if name == self.point and not self._used:
+            self._used = True
+            self.reached.set()
+            self.release.wait(timeout=WAIT_SECONDS)

+class CountingCrm:
+    """An in-process CRM that tells a double put apart from a harmless repeat. capability "keyed": a second put with
+    the same lead id is ALREADY_PRESENT and stores nothing. "blind": it cannot tell, so EVERY put stores one more
+    row. `calls` is the log of every put (lead id, record); `rows` the stored ones, so a double put on either kind
+    shows as len(rows) == 2 (blind) or len(calls) > the allowed number (keyed)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mode: str = "keyed") -> None:
+        if mode not in ("keyed", "blind"):
+            raise ValueError(mode)
+        self.capability = mode
+        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        self.rows: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        # every set_fields call (lead id, email key, CRM owner id, CRM status); kept apart from `calls` because tests
+        # assert on the number of puts there
+        self.set_fields_calls: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    @property
+    def count(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.rows)
+
+    def put(self, lead_id: str, record: Any) -> str:

+    def set_fields(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str, crm_owner_id: str, crm_status: str) -> None:
+        """Logs into set_fields_calls only; a lead with no stored put has no contact (as FakeCrm and HubSpot)."""

+# -- desk builder
+@dataclass
+class Rig:
+    desk: Desk
+    config: Config
+    crm: Any
+    outbox: Any
+    qualifier: RecordedQualifier
+    clock: Clock
+    db_path: Path
+    replies_path: Path
+    desks: list[Desk] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def query(self, sql: str, args: tuple[Any, ...] = ()) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:
+        return rows(self.db_path, sql, args)
+
+    def leads(self) -> int:
+        return int(self.query("SELECT count(*) FROM leads")[0][0])
+
+    def state(self, lead_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+        sql = "SELECT state, last_error FROM followups" + (" WHERE lead_id=?" if lead_id else "")  # noqa: S608
+        r = self.query(sql, (lead_id,) if lead_id else ())
+        assert len(r) == 1, f"expected one follow-up row, got {len(r)}"
+        return r[0][0], r[0][1]
+
+    def restart(self, hooks: Hooks | None = None) -> Desk:
+        """A new Desk on the same lead book and the same fakes, then startup() (the sweep). The old one is closed."""
+        try:
+            self.desk.close()
+        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001, S110 (a crashed desk may fail to close; the file is what matters)
+            pass
+        self.desk = Desk(
+            self.config, self.crm, self.outbox, self.qualifier, hooks=hooks, now=self.clock, schema_sql=None
+        )
+        self.desks.append(self.desk)
+        self.desk.startup()
+        return self.desk
+

+    got_state, got_err = rig.state()

+# (point, outbox, crm) -> (emails, CRM rows, state, last_error). Whatever the point: never more than one email and one

+EXPECT_MORE = {

+    ("L", "keyed", "blind"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("L", "blind", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("L", "blind", "blind"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    # C0: the intent mark is written, the put was never called. A keyed CRM is simply asked; a blind one is not asked
+    # again after a crash (a put may have started), so a person looks and the CRM may hold no row at all.
+    ("C0", "keyed", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("C0", "keyed", "blind"): (0, 0, "unknown", "crm_unconfirmed"),

+    ("C1", "keyed", "blind"): (0, 1, "unknown", "crm_unconfirmed"),  # a blind CRM is never asked twice: a person looks

+    ("D1b", "blind", "keyed"): (0, 1, "unknown", "crash_while_sending"),  # a blind sender is never asked again

+    ("D3", "keyed", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("D3", "keyed", "blind"): (1, 1, "sent", None),

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("crm", ["keyed", "blind"])

+def test_crash_resume_after_label_crm_send_mark_and_result(env, point: str, kind: str, crm: str) -> None:
+    """The moments the first five points leave out: the AI label stored (L), the CRM intent mark written but no put
+    yet (C0), the CRM put came back but crm_done=1 is not written (C1), the send mark written but nothing sent (D1b),
+    the result recorded (D3). CountingCrm logs every put, so a double put shows: on a blind CRM as a second stored
+    row, on a keyed CRM as a third put call (only C1 may legitimately ask a keyed CRM twice)."""
+    hook = CrashAt(point)
+    rig = env.rig(outbox=kind, hooks=hook, crm=CountingCrm(crm))
+    with pytest.raises(SimulatedCrash):
+        rig.desk.handle("form", "sub-1", lead())

+    rig.restart()
+    emails, crm_rows, state, err = EXPECT_MORE[(point, kind, crm)]
+    assert (rig.outbox.count, rig.crm.count) == (emails, crm_rows)
+    allowed_puts = 2 if (crm == "keyed" and point == "C1") else 1
+    assert len(rig.crm.calls) <= allowed_puts, f"{point} {kind} {crm}: double CRM put {rig.crm.calls}"
+    assert len({lid for lid, _ in rig.crm.calls}) <= 1
+    got_state, got_err = rig.state()
+    assert got_state == state and (err is None or got_err == err)
+    assert rig.leads() == 1
+    again = rig.desk.handle("form", "sub-1", lead())  # the caller's retry: a replay, nothing doubled
+    assert again.body["replayed"] is True and again.body["verdict"] == "new"
+    assert (rig.leads(), rig.outbox.count, rig.crm.count) == (1, emails, crm_rows)
+    assert len(rig.crm.calls) <= allowed_puts  # the replay asked the CRM nothing more

+    d, ob = rig.desk, rig.outbox

+    assert d.lead(id1).body["followup"]["sent_at"] is not None
+    assert ob.count == 1

+    again = d.resolve("F" + id1, "sent")

+    assert d.retry("F" + id2).body == {"item_id": "F" + id2, "state": "sent"}
+    assert ob.count == 2

+def fail_until_the_cap(rig: Rig, lid: str, mode: str, err: str) -> None:
+    """The first drive of `lid` just failed with `mode`: the follow-up waits as `pending` (a refused, unreachable or
+    unclear send is tried again by the reaper after 1, 2, 4, 8 s). Make every further try fail the same way until
+    the cap of SEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS tries in all; only then is it `failed`."""
+    assert rig.state(lid) == ("pending", err)
+    for _ in range(SEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1):
+        rig.outbox.fail_next(mode)
+        rig.clock.advance(20)  # longer than the longest wait between tries
+        rig.desk.reap_once()
+    assert rig.state(lid) == ("failed", err)
+

+def test_failed_retry(env) -> None:
+    rig = env.rig(outbox="keyed")
+    d, ob = rig.desk, rig.outbox
+    sent = 0
+    for i, (mode, err) in enumerate([("refuse", "refused"), ("unreachable", "unreachable"), ("drop", "ambiguous")]):
+        ob.fail_next(mode)
+        lid = d.handle("form", f"s{i}", lead(email=f"f{i}@example.test")).body["lead_id"]
+        fail_until_the_cap(rig, lid, mode, err)
+        assert ob.count == sent  # nothing was stored
+        assert any(x["item_id"] == "F" + lid and x["kind"] == "failed" for x in d.review().body)
+        res = d.retry("F" + lid)
+        assert (res.status, res.body) == (200, {"item_id": "F" + lid, "state": "sent"})
+        sent += 1
+        assert ob.count == sent
+    ob.fail_next("record_then_drop")  # keyed: stored, reply lost -> failed/ambiguous; Retry resends the same key
+    lid = d.handle("form", "s9", lead(email="f9@example.test")).body["lead_id"]
+    assert ob.count == sent + 1  # the message is stored although the reply was lost
+    fail_until_the_cap(rig, lid, "drop", "ambiguous")  # every later try also ends unclear (the key makes it safe)
+    assert ob.count == sent + 1
+    assert d.retry("F" + lid).body["state"] == "sent"
+    assert ob.count == sent + 1  # the keyed outbox absorbed the repeat
+    assert ob.keys().count(lid) == 1
+    nr = d.retry("F" + lid)
+    assert (nr.status, nr.body["error"]) == (409, "not_retryable")
+    assert d.retry("FLdoesnotexist").status == 404

+# -- test_retry_twice_concurrent
+def retry_twice_body(rig: Rig) -> None:
+    """Blind outbox; a failed follow-up; two Retry calls released together; the send is slow so they overlap."""
+    d, ob = rig.desk, rig.outbox
+    ob.fail_next("refuse")
+    lid = d.handle("form", "s1", lead()).body["lead_id"]
+    fail_until_the_cap(rig, lid, "refuse", "refused")  # pending after the first refusal, failed after the cap
+    ob.delay = 0.5
+    res = run_threads([lambda: d.retry("F" + lid), lambda: d.retry("F" + lid)])
+    emails = ob.count

+    for r in res:
+        if isinstance(r, BaseException):
+            raise r
+    assert sorted(r.status for r in res) == [200, 409]
+    loser = next(r for r in res if r.status == 409)
+    assert loser.body["error"] in ("in_progress", "not_retryable")
+    assert rig.state(lid)[0] == "sent"

Lambda may not be necessary


A lambda that calls a function without modifying any of its parameters is unnecessary. Python functions are first-class objects and can be passed around in the same way as the resulting lambda. It is recommended to remove the lambda and use the function directly.

+(shortened here); a hung stand-in is released by the test at the end."""

+def wait_for(condition: Callable[[], bool], seconds: float = 10.0) -> bool:
+    """A bounded poll (never an open loop)."""
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        if condition():
+            return True
+        time.sleep(0.02)
+    return condition()
+

+def drive(rig: Any, lid: str) -> None:
+    rig.clock.advance(PLENTY)
+    rig.desk.run_followup(lid)

+class HangCrm(FakeCrm):
+    """A CRM whose put never returns for the lead ids in `hang_ids` until `release` is set (the wait is capped at 8 s so
+    a failing test cannot leave a thread behind for long). `once`: only the first put of a lead hangs."""
+
+    def __init__(self, keyed: bool) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.release = threading.Event()
+        self.hang_ids: set[str] = set()
+        self.once = False
+        self.entered: list[str] = []
+        self._hung: set[str] = set()
+        if keyed:
+            self.capability = "keyed"
+
+    def put(self, lead_id: str, record: Any) -> Any:
+        self.entered.append(lead_id)
+        if lead_id in self.hang_ids and not (self.once and lead_id in self._hung):
+            self._hung.add(lead_id)
+            self.release.wait(8)
+        return super().put(lead_id, record)
+
+
+def hang_outbox(base: type) -> Any:
+    """An outbox whose send never returns for the keys in `hang_ids` until `release` is set; the message is stored when
+    it is released (an abandoned send that completes late). `hang_refresh`: the capability read never returns."""
+
+    class Hangs(base):  # type: ignore[misc, valid-type]
+        def __init__(self) -> None:
+            super().__init__()
+            self.release = threading.Event()
+            self.hang_ids: set[str] = set()
+            self.once = False
+            self.hang_refresh = False
+            self.entered: list[str] = []
+            self.refreshes = 0
+            self._hung: set[str] = set()
+
+        def refresh(self) -> None:
+            self.refreshes += 1
+            if self.hang_refresh:
+                self.release.wait(8)
+
+        def send(self, send_key: str, to: str, subject: str, body: str, timeout: float) -> Any:
+            self.entered.append(send_key)
+            if send_key in self.hang_ids and not (self.once and send_key in self._hung):
+                self._hung.add(send_key)
+                self.release.wait(8)
+            return super().send(send_key, to, subject, body, timeout)
+
+    return Hangs()
+

+    assert rig.desk.resolve(f"F{lid}", "sent").status == 200
+    rig.clock.advance(PLENTY)
+    rig.desk.reap_once()
+    assert outbox.count == 1 and outbox.entered == [lid]

+# The caps: exact, visible, and a full cap does not hide the row

+def test_workers_stay_within_the_cap(env, monkeypatch) -> None:
+    """8 drives ask the model at the same moment: at most the cap of workers is ever started (the slot is taken
+    before the worker starts; a check that only reads a count raised later lets all 8 through)."""
+    rig = env.rig()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(desk_module, "MODEL_CALL_BUDGET_SECONDS", SHORT)
+    started = 0
+    gate_open = threading.Event()
+    lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    class Counted(RecordedQualifier):
+        def qualify(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str) -> Any:
+            nonlocal started
+            with lock:
+                started += 1
+            gate_open.wait(8)
+            return "warm"
+
+    rig.desk.qualifier = Counted(rig.replies_path)
+    parties = 8
+    start = threading.Barrier(parties, timeout=15)
+    outcomes: list[str] = []
+
+    def one() -> None:
+        start.wait()
+        try:
+            rig.desk._ask_model("L0", "a@example.test")
+            outcomes.append("answered")
+        except ModelBusy:
+            outcomes.append("busy")
+        except ModelTimeout:
+            outcomes.append("timeout")
+
+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=one) for _ in range(parties)]
+    for t in threads:
+        t.start()
+    for t in threads:
+        t.join(15)
+    try:
+        assert not any(t.is_alive() for t in threads)
+        assert started == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert sorted(outcomes) == ["busy"] * (parties - gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX) + ["timeout"] * gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert rig.desk.hung_workers()["model"] == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+    finally:
+        gate_open.set()
+    assert wait_for(lambda: drained(rig))
+

+def test_workers_stay_within_the_cap(env, monkeypatch) -> None:
+    """8 drives ask the model at the same moment: at most the cap of workers is ever started (the slot is taken
+    before the worker starts; a check that only reads a count raised later lets all 8 through)."""
+    rig = env.rig()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(desk_module, "MODEL_CALL_BUDGET_SECONDS", SHORT)
+    started = 0
+    gate_open = threading.Event()
+    lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    class Counted(RecordedQualifier):
+        def qualify(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str) -> Any:
+            nonlocal started
+            with lock:
+                started += 1
+            gate_open.wait(8)
+            return "warm"
+
+    rig.desk.qualifier = Counted(rig.replies_path)
+    parties = 8
+    start = threading.Barrier(parties, timeout=15)
+    outcomes: list[str] = []
+
+    def one() -> None:
+        start.wait()
+        try:
+            rig.desk._ask_model("L0", "a@example.test")
+            outcomes.append("answered")
+        except ModelBusy:
+            outcomes.append("busy")
+        except ModelTimeout:
+            outcomes.append("timeout")
+
+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=one) for _ in range(parties)]
+    for t in threads:
+        t.start()
+    for t in threads:
+        t.join(15)
+    try:
+        assert not any(t.is_alive() for t in threads)
+        assert started == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert sorted(outcomes) == ["busy"] * (parties - gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX) + ["timeout"] * gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert rig.desk.hung_workers()["model"] == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+    finally:

+# =====
+# A lock through the result write of a model answer (the real lock path, not a patched one)
+# =====
+class _Hangs(RecordedQualifier):
+    """Hangs for the lead ids in `hang_ids` until `release` is set (capped at 8 s)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: Any) -> None:
+        super().__init__(path)
+        self.release = threading.Event()
+        self.hang_ids: set[str] = set()
+
+    def qualify(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str) -> Any:
+        label = super().qualify(lead_id, email_key)
+        if lead_id in self.hang_ids:
+            self.release.wait(8)
+        return label
+

+def locked_after_answer(env, monkeypatch) -> Iterator[Any]:
+    """A rig whose database is really locked by another connection from the moment the model has answered (once)."""
+    rig = env.rig()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(db, "BUSY_WAIT_SECONDS", 0.05)  # connections opened from now on wait 50 ms, not 5 s
+    monkeypatch.setattr(desk_module, "WRITE_DEADLINE_SECONDS", 0.5)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(desk_module, "GATE_WAIT_SECONDS", 0.2)
+    rig.desk.close()  # this thread's connection is opened again with the short wait
+    holder: dict[str, Any] = {}
+
+    class LocksAfter(RecordedQualifier):
+        lock_next = True
+
+        def qualify(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str) -> Any:
+            label = super().qualify(lead_id, email_key)
+            if self.lock_next:
+                self.lock_next = False
+                other = sqlite3.connect(str(rig.db_path), timeout=0, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
+                other.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")  # holds the write lock until the test lets go
+                holder["conn"] = other
+            return label
+
+    qualifier = LocksAfter(rig.replies_path)
+    rig.desk.qualifier = qualifier
+    holder["rig"] = rig
+
+    def release() -> None:
+        other = holder.pop("conn", None)
+        if other is not None:
+            other.rollback()
+            other.close()
+
+    holder["release"] = release
+    yield holder
+    release()
+

+def wait_until(fn: Callable[[], Any], timeout: float = WAIT_SECONDS, what: str = "condition") -> Any:
+    """Bounded poll. Returns the first truthy value of fn(); raises AssertionError after the timeout."""
+    end = time.monotonic() + timeout

+class Clock:
+    def __init__(self, start: int = 1_700_000_000) -> None:

+class FakeClock:
+    """time.monotonic and time.sleep for the module under test: sleeping moves the clock, nothing really waits."""

+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:  # a pytest MonkeyPatch
+        self.now = 1000.0

+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", self._sleep)

+    def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:
+        # A sleep always moves the clock by a visible step: a wait of 1e-13 added to 1030.0 changes nothing in a

+        # the list makes such a loop fail loudly instead.
+        assert len(self.sleeps) < MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS, "the loop under test never ends"

+class CrashAt(Hooks):

+class CountingCrm:
+    """An in-process CRM that tells a double put apart from a harmless repeat. capability "keyed": a second put with
+    the same lead id is ALREADY_PRESENT and stores nothing. "blind": it cannot tell, so EVERY put stores one more
+    row. `calls` is the log of every put (lead id, record); `rows` the stored ones, so a double put on either kind
+    shows as len(rows) == 2 (blind) or len(calls) > the allowed number (keyed)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mode: str = "keyed") -> None:
+        if mode not in ("keyed", "blind"):
+            raise ValueError(mode)
+        self.capability = mode
+        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        self.rows: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        # every set_fields call (lead id, email key, CRM owner id, CRM status); kept apart from `calls` because tests
+        # assert on the number of puts there
+        self.set_fields_calls: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()

+    @property
+    def count(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.rows)

+    def put(self, lead_id: str, record: Any) -> str:
+        with self._lock:
+            self.calls.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            if self.capability == "keyed" and any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                return "ALREADY_PRESENT"
+            self.rows.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            return "PUT"
+
+    def set_fields(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str, crm_owner_id: str, crm_status: str) -> None:
+        """Logs into set_fields_calls only; a lead with no stored put has no contact (as FakeCrm and HubSpot)."""
+        with self._lock:

+    """Config on tmp_path, in-process fakes, a Desk (started unless start=False). `leadflow` (a dict shaped like the
+    leadflow file, for example a deepcopy of DEMO_LEADFLOW) turns the lead owner, lead stage and reminder feature

+    """Returns (status, parsed JSON). `body` is JSON-encoded; `raw` is sent as is."""
+    data = raw if raw is not None else (None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode())

+def addr(base: str) -> tuple[str, int]:

+def raw_http(base: str, request_bytes: bytes, timeout: float = 10.0) -> bytes:
+    """Send raw bytes on a socket and read until the server ends the connection. A reset after some bytes arrived (the

+    chunks: list[bytes] = []
+    with socket.create_connection(addr(base), timeout=timeout) as s:

+            s.sendall(request_bytes)
+        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):  # the server already answered and closed
+            pass

+            while chunk := s.recv(65536):

+        except ConnectionResetError:

+    barrier = threading.Barrier(len(fns))

+        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (collected and returned to the caller)
+            out[i] = e

+    ts = [threading.Thread(target=wrap, args=(i,)) for i in range(len(fns))]

+def is_write(fn: Any, name: str) -> bool:
+    """True when `fn` (a function handed to `Desk._locked_retry`) belongs to the method or inner function called

+    write named by `where` ("_touch" or "store") once `qualifier.answered` is set."""
+    real = rig.desk._write

+    d = rig.desk
+    by_state = rig.query("SELECT state, last_error, count(*) FROM followups GROUP BY 1, 2")
+    oldest = rig.query(
+        "SELECT lead_id, state, auto_attempts, last_error, updated_at FROM followups WHERE state != 'sent'"
+        " ORDER BY updated_at LIMIT 5"
+    )
+    free = getattr(d._drives, "_free", None)  # noqa: SLF001
+    waiting = len(getattr(d._drives, "_waiters", ()))  # noqa: SLF001
+    return (
+        f"states={by_state}\noldest={oldest}\nnow={d._now()} workers={dict(d._workers)} "  # noqa: SLF001

+def wait_until(fn: Callable[[], Any], timeout: float = WAIT_SECONDS, what: str = "condition") -> Any:
+    """Bounded poll. Returns the first truthy value of fn(); raises AssertionError after the timeout."""
+    end = time.monotonic() + timeout

+class Clock:
+    def __init__(self, start: int = 1_700_000_000) -> None:

+class FakeClock:
+    """time.monotonic and time.sleep for the module under test: sleeping moves the clock, nothing really waits."""

+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:  # a pytest MonkeyPatch
+        self.now = 1000.0

+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "monotonic", lambda: self.now)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", self._sleep)

+    def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:

+class CountingCrm:
+    """An in-process CRM that tells a double put apart from a harmless repeat. capability "keyed": a second put with
+    the same lead id is ALREADY_PRESENT and stores nothing. "blind": it cannot tell, so EVERY put stores one more
+    row. `calls` is the log of every put (lead id, record); `rows` the stored ones, so a double put on either kind
+    shows as len(rows) == 2 (blind) or len(calls) > the allowed number (keyed)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mode: str = "keyed") -> None:
+        if mode not in ("keyed", "blind"):
+            raise ValueError(mode)
+        self.capability = mode
+        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        self.rows: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        # every set_fields call (lead id, email key, CRM owner id, CRM status); kept apart from `calls` because tests
+        # assert on the number of puts there
+        self.set_fields_calls: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()

+    @property
+    def count(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.rows)

+    def put(self, lead_id: str, record: Any) -> str:
+        with self._lock:
+            self.calls.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            if self.capability == "keyed" and any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                return "ALREADY_PRESENT"
+            self.rows.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            return "PUT"

+    def set_fields(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str, crm_owner_id: str, crm_status: str) -> None:
+        """Logs into set_fields_calls only; a lead with no stored put has no contact (as FakeCrm and HubSpot)."""

+def raw_http(base: str, request_bytes: bytes, timeout: float = 10.0) -> bytes:
+    """Send raw bytes on a socket and read until the server ends the connection. A reset after some bytes arrived (the
+    server closed with unread request bytes, as it does for an oversize body) ends the read: what came is returned."""
+    chunks: list[bytes] = []
+    with socket.create_connection(addr(base), timeout=timeout) as s:
+        try:
+            s.sendall(request_bytes)
+        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):  # the server already answered and closed
+            pass

+            while chunk := s.recv(65536):

+        except ConnectionResetError:

+    """Run each fn in its own thread behind one start barrier. Returns results (or the exception object) in order."""
+    barrier = threading.Barrier(len(fns))
+    out: list[Any] = [None] * len(fns)

+    def wrap(i: int) -> None:
+        barrier.wait()
+        try:
+            out[i] = fns[i]()
+        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (collected and returned to the caller)
+            out[i] = e

+    ts = [threading.Thread(target=wrap, args=(i,)) for i in range(len(fns))]

+            def _json(self, status_: int, raw: bytes) -> None:

+    d = rig.desk

+    return (
+        f"states={by_state}\noldest={oldest}\nnow={d._now()} workers={dict(d._workers)} "  # noqa: SLF001

+        self.t += seconds
+

+MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS = 5000  # a loop on the fake clock that sleeps more often than this is stuck
+MIN_FAKE_STEP = 1e-6  # seconds a fake sleep always advances the clock
+
+
+class FakeClock:
+    """time.monotonic and time.sleep for the module under test: sleeping moves the clock, nothing really waits."""
+
+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:  # a pytest MonkeyPatch
+        self.now = 1000.0
+        self.sleeps: list[float] = []
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "monotonic", lambda: self.now)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", self._sleep)
+
+    def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:
+        # A sleep always moves the clock by a visible step: a wait of 1e-13 added to 1030.0 changes nothing in a
+        # float, and a retry loop whose `left` never reaches 0 then never ends. The cap on
+        # the list makes such a loop fail loudly instead.
+        assert len(self.sleeps) < MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS, "the loop under test never ends"
+        self.sleeps.append(seconds)
+        self.now += max(seconds, MIN_FAKE_STEP)

+class LiveClock(Clock):
+    """Whole seconds of real time. For a desk that runs the reaper: the reaper drives a row only when the clock has
+    passed the row's wait, so a frozen Clock would leave every row the request's own drive gave back for ever."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__(int(time.time()))  # wall-clock: the desk's own calendar stamps
+
+    def __call__(self) -> int:
+        return int(time.time())  # wall-clock: the desk's own calendar stamps

+    """Raise SimulatedCrash once at each named point (one-shot per point). An open transaction is rolled back first,
+    as a kill would."""

+    def __init__(self, *points: str) -> None:
+        self.points = set(points)
+        self.fired: list[str] = []
+
+    def crash_point(self, name: str, conn: sqlite3.Connection | None) -> None:
+        if name in self.points and name not in self.fired:
+            self.fired.append(name)
+            if conn is not None and conn.in_transaction:
+                conn.rollback()
+            raise SimulatedCrash(name)
+

+    """Block once at `point` until release is set (holds a receipt open, or a follow-up in `sending`)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, point: str) -> None:
+        self.point = point
+        self.reached = threading.Event()
+        self.release = threading.Event()
+        self._used = False
+
+    def crash_point(self, name: str, conn: sqlite3.Connection | None) -> None:
+        if name == self.point and not self._used:
+            self._used = True
+            self.reached.set()
+            self.release.wait(timeout=WAIT_SECONDS)

+class CountingCrm:
+    """An in-process CRM that tells a double put apart from a harmless repeat. capability "keyed": a second put with
+    the same lead id is ALREADY_PRESENT and stores nothing. "blind": it cannot tell, so EVERY put stores one more
+    row. `calls` is the log of every put (lead id, record); `rows` the stored ones, so a double put on either kind
+    shows as len(rows) == 2 (blind) or len(calls) > the allowed number (keyed)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mode: str = "keyed") -> None:
+        if mode not in ("keyed", "blind"):
+            raise ValueError(mode)
+        self.capability = mode
+        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        self.rows: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        # every set_fields call (lead id, email key, CRM owner id, CRM status); kept apart from `calls` because tests
+        # assert on the number of puts there
+        self.set_fields_calls: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    @property
+    def count(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.rows)
+
+    def put(self, lead_id: str, record: Any) -> str:
+        with self._lock:
+            self.calls.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            if self.capability == "keyed" and any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                return "ALREADY_PRESENT"
+            self.rows.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            return "PUT"
+
+    def set_fields(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str, crm_owner_id: str, crm_status: str) -> None:
+        """Logs into set_fields_calls only; a lead with no stored put has no contact (as FakeCrm and HubSpot)."""
+        with self._lock:
+            self.set_fields_calls.append((lead_id, email_key, crm_owner_id, crm_status))
+            if not any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                raise CrmNothingStored("no contact")
+

+# -- desk builder
+@dataclass
+class Rig:
+    desk: Desk
+    config: Config
+    crm: Any
+    outbox: Any
+    qualifier: RecordedQualifier
+    clock: Clock
+    db_path: Path
+    replies_path: Path
+    desks: list[Desk] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def query(self, sql: str, args: tuple[Any, ...] = ()) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:
+        return rows(self.db_path, sql, args)
+
+    def leads(self) -> int:
+        return int(self.query("SELECT count(*) FROM leads")[0][0])
+
+    def state(self, lead_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+        sql = "SELECT state, last_error FROM followups" + (" WHERE lead_id=?" if lead_id else "")  # noqa: S608
+        r = self.query(sql, (lead_id,) if lead_id else ())
+        assert len(r) == 1, f"expected one follow-up row, got {len(r)}"
+        return r[0][0], r[0][1]
+
+    def restart(self, hooks: Hooks | None = None) -> Desk:
+        """A new Desk on the same lead book and the same fakes, then startup() (the sweep). The old one is closed."""
+        try:
+            self.desk.close()
+        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001, S110 (a crashed desk may fail to close; the file is what matters)
+            pass
+        self.desk = Desk(
+            self.config, self.crm, self.outbox, self.qualifier, hooks=hooks, now=self.clock, schema_sql=None

+    leadflow: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
+    outbox_kind: str | None = None,
+    crm_kind: str | None = None,
+    **config_over: Any,
+) -> Rig:
+    """Config on tmp_path, in-process fakes, a Desk (started unless start=False). `leadflow` (a dict shaped like the
+    leadflow file, for example a deepcopy of DEMO_LEADFLOW) turns the lead owner, lead stage and reminder feature
+    on: it is written to tmp_path and read back by the real parser, so a test can never build a Leadflow the desk
+    would refuse. None (the default) leaves the feature off."""
+    if outbox_kind is not None:  # the sender KIND the Config names (`outbox` is the sender object)
+        config_over["outbox"] = outbox_kind
+    if crm_kind is not None:  # the CRM KIND the Config names (`crm` is the CRM object)
+        config_over["crm"] = crm_kind
+    replies_path = tmp_path / "replies.json"
+    replies_path.write_text(json.dumps(replies or {}), encoding="utf-8")
+    if leadflow is not None:
+        flow_path = tmp_path / "leadflow.json"
+        flow_path.write_text(json.dumps(leadflow), encoding="utf-8")
+        lf = read_leadflow(flow_path)
+        config_over.setdefault("leadflow_path", flow_path)
+        config_over["leadflow"] = lf
+        config_over.setdefault("nudge_to", NUDGE_TO_TEST if lf.nudge_after_seconds is not None else "")
+    config = Config(db_path=tmp_path / "desk.sqlite3", port=0, replies_path=replies_path, **config_over)
+    ob = {"keyed": KeyedOutbox, "blind": BlindOutbox}[outbox]() if isinstance(outbox, str) else outbox
+    crm, qual, clock = crm or FakeCrm(), RecordedQualifier(replies_path), clock or Clock()
+    desk = Desk(config, crm, ob, qual, hooks=hooks, now=clock, schema_sql=schema_sql)

+# -- HTTP helpers
+_OPENER = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))

+def call(base: str, method: str, path: str, body: Any = None, raw: bytes | None = None, timeout: float = 30.0) -> Any:
+    """Returns (status, parsed JSON). `body` is JSON-encoded; `raw` is sent as is."""
+    data = raw if raw is not None else (None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode())
+    req = urllib.request.Request(base + path, data=data, method=method)  # noqa: S310 (loopback test URL)
+    if data is not None:
+        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
+    try:
+        with _OPENER.open(req, timeout=timeout) as r:  # noqa: S310
+            return r.status, json.loads(r.read().decode() or "null")
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+        return e.code, json.loads(e.read().decode() or "null")

+def post_lead(base: str, source: str, ref: str, payload: Any) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
+    return call(base, "POST", "/leads", {"source": source, "source_ref": ref, "payload": payload})  # type: ignore[no-any-return]

+def addr(base: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
+    """(host, port) of a base URL such as http://127.0.0.1:8080."""
+    host, port = base.removeprefix("http://").split(":")
+    return host, int(port)
+
+
+def raw_http(base: str, request_bytes: bytes, timeout: float = 10.0) -> bytes:
+    """Send raw bytes on a socket and read until the server ends the connection. A reset after some bytes arrived (the
+    server closed with unread request bytes, as it does for an oversize body) ends the read: what came is returned."""
+    chunks: list[bytes] = []
+    with socket.create_connection(addr(base), timeout=timeout) as s:
+        try:
+            s.sendall(request_bytes)
+        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):  # the server already answered and closed
+            pass
+        try:
+            while chunk := s.recv(65536):
+                chunks.append(chunk)
+        except ConnectionResetError:
+            pass
+    return b"".join(chunks)
+
+
+def raw_exchange(base: str, request_bytes: bytes, timeout: float = 10.0) -> tuple[int, Any]:
+    """Send raw bytes on a socket, read to the end of the connection, return (status, JSON body)."""
+    data = raw_http(base, request_bytes, timeout)
+    head, _, body = data.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
+    status = int(head.split(b" ", 2)[1])
+    return status, json.loads(body.decode() or "null")

+def run_threads(fns: list[Callable[[], Any]]) -> list[Any]:
+    """Run each fn in its own thread behind one start barrier. Returns results (or the exception object) in order."""
+    barrier = threading.Barrier(len(fns))
+    out: list[Any] = [None] * len(fns)
+
+    def wrap(i: int) -> None:
+        barrier.wait()
+        try:
+            out[i] = fns[i]()
+        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (collected and returned to the caller)
+            out[i] = e
+
+    ts = [threading.Thread(target=wrap, args=(i,)) for i in range(len(fns))]
+    for t in ts:
+        t.start()
+    for t in ts:
+        t.join(timeout=60)
+    return out

+    if p.poll() is None:

+def is_write(fn: Any, name: str) -> bool:
+    """True when `fn` (a function handed to `Desk._locked_retry`) belongs to the method or inner function called
+    `name`. Whole dotted parts are compared, never a substring, and a test that selects a fault this way must also
+    assert that the fault fired (a rename would otherwise turn the test into a silent no-op)."""
+    return name in fn.__qualname__.split(".")

+    real = rig.desk._write

+# -- helpers
+class ConnProxy:
+    """A sqlite3 connection that runs `rules` (functions of the SQL text) before every execute. A rule may sleep or
+    raise. Everything else is passed through to the real connection."""
+
+    def __init__(self, real: sqlite3.Connection, rules: list[Any]) -> None:
+        self._c = real
+        self._rules = rules
+
+    def execute(self, sql: str, *args: Any) -> Any:
+        for rule in self._rules:
+            rule(sql)
+        return self._c.execute(sql, *args)
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
+        return getattr(self._c, name)
+
+
+def patch_connect(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, *rules: Any) -> None:
+    real = db.connect
+    monkeypatch.setattr(db, "connect", lambda p: ConnProxy(real(p), list(rules)))
+
+
+def fail_when(match: str, exc: Exception, times: int | None = None, armed: list[bool] | None = None) -> Any:
+    """Rule: raise exc for an execute whose SQL contains `match` (`times` times, or while armed[0])."""
+    left = [times]
+    lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    def rule(sql: str) -> None:
+        if match not in sql:
+            return
+        with lock:
+            if armed is not None and not armed[0]:
+                return
+            if left[0] is not None:
+                if left[0] <= 0:
+                    return
+                left[0] -= 1
+        raise exc
+
+    return rule
+
+
+def busy() -> sqlite3.OperationalError:
+    return sqlite3.OperationalError("database is locked")

+    con.execute("UPDATE followups SET state=? WHERE lead_id=?", (state, lid))
+    con.close()

+    r = rows(
+        path,
+        "SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM receipts WHERE outcome IS NULL), (SELECT count(*) FROM leads),"
+        " (SELECT count(*) FROM followups WHERE state='sending'),"
+        " (SELECT count(*) FROM followups WHERE state='pending'),"
+        " (SELECT count(*) FROM followups WHERE state='sent'), (SELECT count(*) FROM followups WHERE state='failed'),"
+        " (SELECT count(*) FROM followups WHERE state='unknown')",

+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:

+def _bare_casts(source: str) -> list[int]:

+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """A direct-only scan (the contrast for the full one): a cast whose own argument

+ENV_NAMES = {
+    "env",
+    "environ",
+    "config_env",

+CASTS = {"int", "float", "Decimal"}

+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """A direct-only scan (the contrast for the full one): a cast whose own argument
+    mentions an env name, a Subscript/Call on one, or `.environ` / `getenv`."""
+    hits = []
+    for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id in CASTS and n.args:
+            for m in ast.walk(n.args[0]):
+                if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript | ast.Call):
+                    base = m.value if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) else getattr(m.func, "value", None)
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Name) and base.id in ENV_NAMES:
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Attribute) and base.attr == "environ":
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+    return hits
+
+
+def _is_cast_expr(node: ast.AST, aliases: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """int, float, Decimal, decimal.Decimal, builtins.int, an alias of one, or functools.partial(<one of these>)."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
+        return node.id in CASTS or node.id in aliases
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
+        return node.attr in CASTS
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
+        fn = node.func
+        is_partial = (isinstance(fn, ast.Name) and fn.id == "partial") or (
+            isinstance(fn, ast.Attribute) and fn.attr == "partial"
+        )
+        return is_partial and bool(node.args) and _is_cast_expr(node.args[0], aliases)
+    return False
+
+
+def _cast_aliases(tree: ast.AST) -> set[str]:
+    """Names that stand for a number cast: `_i = int`, `conv = functools.partial(int)`, `from decimal import Decimal
+    as D`, `from builtins import int as I`."""
+    aliases: set[str] = set()
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for n in ast.walk(tree):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module in ("decimal", "builtins"):
+                for a in n.names:
+                    if a.name in CASTS and (a.asname or a.name) not in aliases and a.asname:
+                        aliases.add(a.asname)
+                        changed = True
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and _is_cast_expr(n.value, aliases):
+                for tgt in n.targets:
+                    if isinstance(tgt, ast.Name) and tgt.id not in aliases:
+                        aliases.add(tgt.id)
+                        changed = True
+    return aliases
+
+
+def _scopes(tree: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The module and every function."""
+    return [tree, *[n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)]]

+    that looks like a setting name (`cfg["DESK_PORT"]`), whatever the mapping is called."""

The method doesn't use its bound instance. Read more about staticmethods [here](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#staticmethod).

+def fail_until_the_cap(rig: Rig, lid: str, mode: str, err: str) -> None:

+def test_write_once_triggers(env) -> None:
+    rig = env.rig()
+    d = rig.desk
+    first = d.handle("form", "sub-1", lead())
+    lead_id = first.body["lead_id"]

+    con = sqlite3.connect(rig.db_path, isolation_level=None)
+    con.execute("PRAGMA recursive_triggers=ON")  # REPLACE only fires the delete trigger with this on

+    try:
+
+        def refused(sql: str, text: str) -> None:
+            with pytest.raises(sqlite3.DatabaseError, match=text):
+                con.execute(sql)
+
+        refused("UPDATE receipts SET payload='{}'", "never change")
+        refused("UPDATE receipts SET source_ref='x'", "never change")
+        refused("UPDATE receipts SET received_at=1", "never change")
+        refused("UPDATE receipts SET outcome='review'", "written once")
+        refused("UPDATE receipts SET outcome_reason='x', decided_at=1", "written once")
+        refused("DELETE FROM receipts", "never deleted")
+        refused(
+            "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO receipts(source, source_ref, received_at, payload) VALUES('form','sub-1',1,'{}')",
+            "never deleted",
+        )
+        refused("UPDATE leads SET name='x'", "write-once")
+        refused("DELETE FROM leads", "write-once")
+        refused(

+        )
+        refused("UPDATE followups SET state='failed'", "final")  # the follow-up is `sent` by now

+        refused(

+EXPECT: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[int, str, str | None]] = {

+def test_crash_resume_each_point(env, point: str, kind: str, crm: str) -> None:
+    hook = CrashAt(point)
+    rig = env.rig(outbox=kind, hooks=hook, crm=CountingCrm(crm))
+    with pytest.raises(SimulatedCrash):
+        rig.desk.handle("form", "sub-1", lead())
+    assert hook.fired == [point]  # the point really was reached
+    rig.restart()  # a new Desk on the same file: the start-up sweep
+    emails, state, err = EXPECT[(point, kind)]
+    assert rig.outbox.count == emails, f"{point} {kind}: emails"
+    assert rig.leads() == 1
+    assert rig.crm.count == 1
+    assert len(rig.crm.calls) <= 1, f"{point} {kind} {crm}: the CRM was asked {len(rig.crm.calls)} times"
+    got_state, got_err = rig.state()
+    assert got_state == state
+    if err:
+        assert got_err == err
+    # the caller's retry of the same request id: replay, no second lead, no second email
+    r = rig.desk.handle("form", "sub-1", lead())
+    assert r.body["replayed"] is True
+    assert r.body["verdict"] == "new"
+    assert rig.leads() == 1
+    assert rig.outbox.count == emails

+# (point, outbox, crm) -> (emails, CRM rows, state, last_error). Whatever the point: never more than one email and one
+# CRM row, and a state a person can read.
+EXPECT_MORE = {
+    ("L", "keyed", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("L", "keyed", "blind"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("L", "blind", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("L", "blind", "blind"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    # C0: the intent mark is written, the put was never called. A keyed CRM is simply asked; a blind one is not asked
+    # again after a crash (a put may have started), so a person looks and the CRM may hold no row at all.
+    ("C0", "keyed", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("C0", "keyed", "blind"): (0, 0, "unknown", "crm_unconfirmed"),
+    ("C0", "blind", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("C0", "blind", "blind"): (0, 0, "unknown", "crm_unconfirmed"),
+    ("C1", "keyed", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),  # a keyed CRM is simply asked again with the same key
+    ("C1", "keyed", "blind"): (0, 1, "unknown", "crm_unconfirmed"),  # a blind CRM is never asked twice: a person looks
+    ("C1", "blind", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("C1", "blind", "blind"): (0, 1, "unknown", "crm_unconfirmed"),
+    ("D1b", "keyed", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),  # the send mark was written, nothing left: a keyed sender goes on
+    ("D1b", "keyed", "blind"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("D1b", "blind", "keyed"): (0, 1, "unknown", "crash_while_sending"),  # a blind sender is never asked again

+    ("D3", "keyed", "keyed"): (1, 1, "sent", None),
+    ("D3", "keyed", "blind"): (1, 1, "sent", None),

+def test_crash_resume_after_label_crm_send_mark_and_result(env, point: str, kind: str, crm: str) -> None:
+    """The moments the first five points leave out: the AI label stored (L), the CRM intent mark written but no put
+    yet (C0), the CRM put came back but crm_done=1 is not written (C1), the send mark written but nothing sent (D1b),
+    the result recorded (D3). CountingCrm logs every put, so a double put shows: on a blind CRM as a second stored
+    row, on a keyed CRM as a third put call (only C1 may legitimately ask a keyed CRM twice)."""
+    hook = CrashAt(point)
+    rig = env.rig(outbox=kind, hooks=hook, crm=CountingCrm(crm))
+    with pytest.raises(SimulatedCrash):

+    assert (rig.outbox.count, rig.crm.count) == (emails, crm_rows)
+    allowed_puts = 2 if (crm == "keyed" and point == "C1") else 1
+    assert len(rig.crm.calls) <= allowed_puts, f"{point} {kind} {crm}: double CRM put {rig.crm.calls}"
+    assert len({lid for lid, _ in rig.crm.calls}) <= 1

+    assert rig.leads() == 1
+    again = rig.desk.handle("form", "sub-1", lead())  # the caller's retry: a replay, nothing doubled
+    assert again.body["replayed"] is True and again.body["verdict"] == "new"
+    assert (rig.leads(), rig.outbox.count, rig.crm.count) == (1, emails, crm_rows)
+    assert len(rig.crm.calls) <= allowed_puts  # the replay asked the CRM nothing more

+def fail_until_the_cap(rig: Rig, lid: str, mode: str, err: str) -> None:
+    """The first drive of `lid` just failed with `mode`: the follow-up waits as `pending` (a refused, unreachable or
+    unclear send is tried again by the reaper after 1, 2, 4, 8 s). Make every further try fail the same way until
+    the cap of SEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS tries in all; only then is it `failed`."""
+    assert rig.state(lid) == ("pending", err)
+    for _ in range(SEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1):
+        rig.outbox.fail_next(mode)
+        rig.clock.advance(20)  # longer than the longest wait between tries
+        rig.desk.reap_once()
+    assert rig.state(lid) == ("failed", err)

Lambda may not be necessary


A lambda that calls a function without modifying any of its parameters is unnecessary. Python functions are first-class objects and can be passed around in the same way as the resulting lambda. It is recommended to remove the lambda and use the function directly.

+        def send(self, send_key: str, to: str, subject: str, body: str, timeout: float) -> Any:
+            self.entered.append(send_key)
+            if send_key in self.hang_ids and not (self.once and send_key in self._hung):
+                self._hung.add(send_key)
+                self.release.wait(8)
+            return super().send(send_key, to, subject, body, timeout)
+
+    return Hangs()

+def test_workers_stay_within_the_cap(env, monkeypatch) -> None:
+    """8 drives ask the model at the same moment: at most the cap of workers is ever started (the slot is taken
+    before the worker starts; a check that only reads a count raised later lets all 8 through)."""
+    rig = env.rig()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(desk_module, "MODEL_CALL_BUDGET_SECONDS", SHORT)
+    started = 0
+    gate_open = threading.Event()
+    lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    class Counted(RecordedQualifier):
+        def qualify(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str) -> Any:
+            nonlocal started
+            with lock:
+                started += 1
+            gate_open.wait(8)
+            return "warm"
+
+    rig.desk.qualifier = Counted(rig.replies_path)
+    parties = 8
+    start = threading.Barrier(parties, timeout=15)
+    outcomes: list[str] = []
+
+    def one() -> None:
+        start.wait()
+        try:
+            rig.desk._ask_model("L0", "a@example.test")
+            outcomes.append("answered")
+        except ModelBusy:
+            outcomes.append("busy")
+        except ModelTimeout:
+            outcomes.append("timeout")
+
+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=one) for _ in range(parties)]
+    for t in threads:
+        t.start()
+    for t in threads:
+        t.join(15)
+    try:
+        assert not any(t.is_alive() for t in threads)
+        assert started == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert sorted(outcomes) == ["busy"] * (parties - gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX) + ["timeout"] * gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert rig.desk.hung_workers()["model"] == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+    finally:
+        gate_open.set()
+    assert wait_for(lambda: drained(rig))
+

+def test_workers_stay_within_the_cap(env, monkeypatch) -> None:
+    """8 drives ask the model at the same moment: at most the cap of workers is ever started (the slot is taken
+    before the worker starts; a check that only reads a count raised later lets all 8 through)."""
+    rig = env.rig()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(desk_module, "MODEL_CALL_BUDGET_SECONDS", SHORT)
+    started = 0
+    gate_open = threading.Event()
+    lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    class Counted(RecordedQualifier):
+        def qualify(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str) -> Any:
+            nonlocal started
+            with lock:
+                started += 1
+            gate_open.wait(8)
+            return "warm"
+
+    rig.desk.qualifier = Counted(rig.replies_path)
+    parties = 8
+    start = threading.Barrier(parties, timeout=15)
+    outcomes: list[str] = []
+
+    def one() -> None:
+        start.wait()
+        try:
+            rig.desk._ask_model("L0", "a@example.test")
+            outcomes.append("answered")
+        except ModelBusy:
+            outcomes.append("busy")
+        except ModelTimeout:
+            outcomes.append("timeout")
+
+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=one) for _ in range(parties)]
+    for t in threads:
+        t.start()
+    for t in threads:
+        t.join(15)
+    try:
+        assert not any(t.is_alive() for t in threads)
+        assert started == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert sorted(outcomes) == ["busy"] * (parties - gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX) + ["timeout"] * gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert rig.desk.hung_workers()["model"] == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+    finally:
+        gate_open.set()

+# =====
+# A lock through the result write of a model answer (the real lock path, not a patched one)
+# =====
+class _Hangs(RecordedQualifier):
+    """Hangs for the lead ids in `hang_ids` until `release` is set (capped at 8 s)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: Any) -> None:
+        super().__init__(path)
+        self.release = threading.Event()
+        self.hang_ids: set[str] = set()
+
+    def qualify(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str) -> Any:
+        label = super().qualify(lead_id, email_key)
+        if lead_id in self.hang_ids:
+            self.release.wait(8)
+        return label
+

+@pytest.fixture
+def locked_after_answer(env, monkeypatch) -> Iterator[Any]:
+    """A rig whose database is really locked by another connection from the moment the model has answered (once)."""
+    rig = env.rig()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(db, "BUSY_WAIT_SECONDS", 0.05)  # connections opened from now on wait 50 ms, not 5 s
+    monkeypatch.setattr(desk_module, "WRITE_DEADLINE_SECONDS", 0.5)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(desk_module, "GATE_WAIT_SECONDS", 0.2)
+    rig.desk.close()  # this thread's connection is opened again with the short wait
+    holder: dict[str, Any] = {}
+
+    class LocksAfter(RecordedQualifier):
+        lock_next = True
+
+        def qualify(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str) -> Any:
+            label = super().qualify(lead_id, email_key)
+            if self.lock_next:
+                self.lock_next = False
+                other = sqlite3.connect(str(rig.db_path), timeout=0, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
+                other.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")  # holds the write lock until the test lets go
+                holder["conn"] = other
+            return label
+
+    qualifier = LocksAfter(rig.replies_path)
+    rig.desk.qualifier = qualifier
+    holder["rig"] = rig
+
+    def release() -> None:
+        other = holder.pop("conn", None)
+        if other is not None:
+            other.rollback()
+            other.close()
+
+    holder["release"] = release
+    yield holder
+    release()
+

+def lead_ids_containing(monkeypatch: Any, fragment: str) -> None:
+    """Every lead number made from now on holds `fragment` in its random hex part (a random draw can do this by
+    chance: "L" and 12 hex characters can spell ada, bad, face...). Lets a test prove that a probe made of hex letters
+    never decides its result by chance. Only the 6-byte token of a lead number is changed."""
+    real, counter = secrets.token_hex, itertools.count()
+
+    def forced(nbytes: int | None = None) -> str:
+        if nbytes != 6:  # LEAD_ID_HEX_CHARS // 2: the lead number
+            return real(nbytes)
+        return fragment + f"{next(counter):0{12 - len(fragment)}d}"  # unique: the counter fills the rest

+def reset_on_close(sock: socket.socket) -> None:

+def wait_until(fn: Callable[[], Any], timeout: float = WAIT_SECONDS, what: str = "condition") -> Any:
+    """Bounded poll. Returns the first truthy value of fn(); raises AssertionError after the timeout."""
+    end = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while True:
+        try:
+            val = fn()
+        except (OSError, ValueError):
+            val = None
+        if val:
+            return val
+        if time.monotonic() > end:
+            raise AssertionError(f"timed out waiting for {what}")
+        time.sleep(0.05)

+# -- clock and hooks
+class Clock:
+    def __init__(self, start: int = 1_700_000_000) -> None:
+        self.t = start
+
+    def __call__(self) -> int:
+        return self.t
+
+    def advance(self, seconds: int) -> None:
+        self.t += seconds
+

+MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS = 5000  # a loop on the fake clock that sleeps more often than this is stuck
+MIN_FAKE_STEP = 1e-6  # seconds a fake sleep always advances the clock
+

+class FakeClock:
+    """time.monotonic and time.sleep for the module under test: sleeping moves the clock, nothing really waits."""
+
+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:  # a pytest MonkeyPatch
+        self.now = 1000.0
+        self.sleeps: list[float] = []
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "monotonic", lambda: self.now)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", self._sleep)
+
+    def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:
+        # A sleep always moves the clock by a visible step: a wait of 1e-13 added to 1030.0 changes nothing in a
+        # float, and a retry loop whose `left` never reaches 0 then never ends. The cap on
+        # the list makes such a loop fail loudly instead.
+        assert len(self.sleeps) < MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS, "the loop under test never ends"
+        self.sleeps.append(seconds)
+        self.now += max(seconds, MIN_FAKE_STEP)

+class LiveClock(Clock):
+    """Whole seconds of real time. For a desk that runs the reaper: the reaper drives a row only when the clock has
+    passed the row's wait, so a frozen Clock would leave every row the request's own drive gave back for ever."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__(int(time.time()))  # wall-clock: the desk's own calendar stamps
+
+    def __call__(self) -> int:
+        return int(time.time())  # wall-clock: the desk's own calendar stamps

+class CrashAt(Hooks):
+    """Raise SimulatedCrash once at each named point (one-shot per point). An open transaction is rolled back first,
+    as a kill would."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *points: str) -> None:
+        self.points = set(points)
+        self.fired: list[str] = []
+
+    def crash_point(self, name: str, conn: sqlite3.Connection | None) -> None:
+        if name in self.points and name not in self.fired:
+            self.fired.append(name)
+            if conn is not None and conn.in_transaction:
+                conn.rollback()
+            raise SimulatedCrash(name)
+
+
+class BlockAt(Hooks):
+    """Block once at `point` until release is set (holds a receipt open, or a follow-up in `sending`)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, point: str) -> None:
+        self.point = point
+        self.reached = threading.Event()
+        self.release = threading.Event()
+        self._used = False
+
+    def crash_point(self, name: str, conn: sqlite3.Connection | None) -> None:
+        if name == self.point and not self._used:
+            self._used = True
+            self.reached.set()
+            self.release.wait(timeout=WAIT_SECONDS)
+
+
+class CountingCrm:
+    """An in-process CRM that tells a double put apart from a harmless repeat. capability "keyed": a second put with
+    the same lead id is ALREADY_PRESENT and stores nothing. "blind": it cannot tell, so EVERY put stores one more
+    row. `calls` is the log of every put (lead id, record); `rows` the stored ones, so a double put on either kind
+    shows as len(rows) == 2 (blind) or len(calls) > the allowed number (keyed)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mode: str = "keyed") -> None:
+        if mode not in ("keyed", "blind"):
+            raise ValueError(mode)
+        self.capability = mode
+        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        self.rows: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        # every set_fields call (lead id, email key, CRM owner id, CRM status); kept apart from `calls` because tests
+        # assert on the number of puts there
+        self.set_fields_calls: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    @property
+    def count(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.rows)
+
+    def put(self, lead_id: str, record: Any) -> str:
+        with self._lock:
+            self.calls.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            if self.capability == "keyed" and any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                return "ALREADY_PRESENT"
+            self.rows.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            return "PUT"
+
+    def set_fields(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str, crm_owner_id: str, crm_status: str) -> None:
+        """Logs into set_fields_calls only; a lead with no stored put has no contact (as FakeCrm and HubSpot)."""
+        with self._lock:
+            self.set_fields_calls.append((lead_id, email_key, crm_owner_id, crm_status))
+            if not any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                raise CrmNothingStored("no contact")
+
