+# -- desk builder
+@dataclass
+class Rig:
+    desk: Desk
+    config: Config
+    crm: Any
+    outbox: Any
+    qualifier: RecordedQualifier
+    clock: Clock
+    db_path: Path
+    replies_path: Path
+    desks: list[Desk] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def query(self, sql: str, args: tuple[Any, ...] = ()) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:
+        return rows(self.db_path, sql, args)
+
+    def leads(self) -> int:
+        return int(self.query("SELECT count(*) FROM leads")[0][0])
+
+    def state(self, lead_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+        sql = "SELECT state, last_error FROM followups" + (" WHERE lead_id=?" if lead_id else "")  # noqa: S608
+        r = self.query(sql, (lead_id,) if lead_id else ())
+        assert len(r) == 1, f"expected one follow-up row, got {len(r)}"
+        return r[0][0], r[0][1]
+
+    def restart(self, hooks: Hooks | None = None) -> Desk:
+        """A new Desk on the same lead book and the same fakes, then startup() (the sweep). The old one is closed."""
+        try:
+            self.desk.close()
+        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001, S110 (a crashed desk may fail to close; the file is what matters)
+            pass
+        self.desk = Desk(
+            self.config, self.crm, self.outbox, self.qualifier, hooks=hooks, now=self.clock, schema_sql=None
+        )
+        self.desks.append(self.desk)
+        self.desk.startup()
+        return self.desk
+
+
+def rows(db_path: Path, sql: str, args: tuple[Any, ...] = ()) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:
+    con = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=10)
+    try:
+        return con.execute(sql, args).fetchall()
+    finally:
+        con.close()
+
+
+def build_rig(
+    tmp_path: Path,
+    outbox: str | Any = "keyed",
+    hooks: Hooks | None = None,
+    schema_sql: str | None = None,
+    replies: dict[str, str] | None = None,
+    start: bool = True,
+    clock: Clock | None = None,
+    crm: Any = None,
+    leadflow: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
+    outbox_kind: str | None = None,
+    crm_kind: str | None = None,
+    **config_over: Any,
+) -> Rig:
+    """Config on tmp_path, in-process fakes, a Desk (started unless start=False). `leadflow` (a dict shaped like the
+    leadflow file, for example a deepcopy of DEMO_LEADFLOW) turns the lead owner, lead stage and reminder feature
+    on: it is written to tmp_path and read back by the real parser, so a test can never build a Leadflow the desk
+    would refuse. None (the default) leaves the feature off."""
+    if outbox_kind is not None:  # the sender KIND the Config names (`outbox` is the sender object)
+        config_over["outbox"] = outbox_kind
+    if crm_kind is not None:  # the CRM KIND the Config names (`crm` is the CRM object)
+        config_over["crm"] = crm_kind
+    replies_path = tmp_path / "replies.json"
+    replies_path.write_text(json.dumps(replies or {}), encoding="utf-8")
+    if leadflow is not None:
+        flow_path = tmp_path / "leadflow.json"
+        flow_path.write_text(json.dumps(leadflow), encoding="utf-8")
+        lf = read_leadflow(flow_path)
+        config_over.setdefault("leadflow_path", flow_path)
+        config_over["leadflow"] = lf
+        config_over.setdefault("nudge_to", NUDGE_TO_TEST if lf.nudge_after_seconds is not None else "")
+    config = Config(db_path=tmp_path / "desk.sqlite3", port=0, replies_path=replies_path, **config_over)
+    ob = {"keyed": KeyedOutbox, "blind": BlindOutbox}[outbox]() if isinstance(outbox, str) else outbox
+    crm, qual, clock = crm or FakeCrm(), RecordedQualifier(replies_path), clock or Clock()
+    desk = Desk(config, crm, ob, qual, hooks=hooks, now=clock, schema_sql=schema_sql)
+    rig = Rig(desk, config, crm, ob, qual, clock, config.db_path, replies_path, [desk])
+    if start:
+        desk.startup()
+    return rig
+
+
+# -- HTTP helpers
+_OPENER = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
+
+
+def call(base: str, method: str, path: str, body: Any = None, raw: bytes | None = None, timeout: float = 30.0) -> Any:
+    """Returns (status, parsed JSON). `body` is JSON-encoded; `raw` is sent as is."""
+    data = raw if raw is not None else (None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode())
+    req = urllib.request.Request(base + path, data=data, method=method)  # noqa: S310 (loopback test URL)
+    if data is not None:
+        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
+    try:
+        with _OPENER.open(req, timeout=timeout) as r:  # noqa: S310
+            return r.status, json.loads(r.read().decode() or "null")
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+        return e.code, json.loads(e.read().decode() or "null")
+
+
+def post_lead(base: str, source: str, ref: str, payload: Any) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
+    return call(base, "POST", "/leads", {"source": source, "source_ref": ref, "payload": payload})  # type: ignore[no-any-return]
+
+
+def addr(base: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
+    """(host, port) of a base URL such as http://127.0.0.1:8080."""
+    host, port = base.removeprefix("http://").split(":")
+    return host, int(port)
+
+
+def raw_http(base: str, request_bytes: bytes, timeout: float = 10.0) -> bytes:
+    """Send raw bytes on a socket and read until the server ends the connection. A reset after some bytes arrived (the
+    server closed with unread request bytes, as it does for an oversize body) ends the read: what came is returned."""
+    chunks: list[bytes] = []
+    with socket.create_connection(addr(base), timeout=timeout) as s:
+        try:
+            s.sendall(request_bytes)
+        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):  # the server already answered and closed
+            pass
+        try:
+            while chunk := s.recv(65536):
+                chunks.append(chunk)
+        except ConnectionResetError:
+            pass
+    return b"".join(chunks)
+
+
+def raw_exchange(base: str, request_bytes: bytes, timeout: float = 10.0) -> tuple[int, Any]:
+    """Send raw bytes on a socket, read to the end of the connection, return (status, JSON body)."""
+    data = raw_http(base, request_bytes, timeout)
+    head, _, body = data.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
+    status = int(head.split(b" ", 2)[1])
+    return status, json.loads(body.decode() or "null")
+
+
+def run_threads(fns: list[Callable[[], Any]]) -> list[Any]:
+    """Run each fn in its own thread behind one start barrier. Returns results (or the exception object) in order."""
+    barrier = threading.Barrier(len(fns))
+    out: list[Any] = [None] * len(fns)
+
+    def wrap(i: int) -> None:
+        barrier.wait()
+        try:
+            out[i] = fns[i]()
+        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (collected and returned to the caller)
+            out[i] = e
+
+    ts = [threading.Thread(target=wrap, args=(i,)) for i in range(len(fns))]
+    for t in ts:
+        t.start()
+    for t in ts:
+        t.join(timeout=60)
+    return out
+
+
+# -- a tiny stand-in sender with scripted misbehaviour (for test_error_mapping)
+class StubSender:
+    """Serves GET /fake/info normally; POST /fake/outbox does what `behaviour` says."""
+
+    def __init__(self, behaviour: str, status: int = 200, body: bytes = b"{}") -> None:
+        outer = self
+
+        class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+            def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None:  # noqa: A002
+                return None
+
+            def _json(self, status_: int, raw: bytes) -> None:
+                self.send_response(status_)
+                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(raw)))
+                self.send_header("Connection", "close")
+                self.end_headers()
+                self.wfile.write(raw)
+
+            def do_GET(self) -> None:
+                self._json(200, json.dumps({"outbox_capability": "keyed", "mode": "keyed"}).encode())
+
+            def do_POST(self) -> None:
+                n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
+                self.rfile.read(n)
+                if outer.behaviour == "status":
+                    return self._json(outer.status, outer.body)
+                if outer.behaviour == "reset":  # TCP reset instead of a reply
+                    reset_on_close(self.connection)
+                    self.close_connection = True
+                    self.connection.close()
+                    return None
+                if outer.behaviour == "garbage":
+                    return self._json(200, b"this is not json")
+                return None
+
+        self.behaviour, self.status, self.body = behaviour, status, body
+        self.srv = ThreadingHTTPServer((HOST, 0), H)
+        self.srv.daemon_threads = True
+        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.srv.serve_forever, daemon=True)
+        self.thread.start()
+        self.url = f"http://{HOST}:{self.srv.server_address[1]}"
+
+    def stop(self) -> None:
+        self.srv.shutdown()
+        self.srv.server_close()
+        self.thread.join(timeout=5)
+
+
+# -- subprocess helpers
+def start_proc(args: list[str], env: dict[str, str]) -> subprocess.Popen[bytes]:
+    return subprocess.Popen(  # noqa: S603 (this repository's interpreter and modules)
+        [sys.executable, *args], cwd=REPO, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT
+    )
+
+
+def stop_proc(p: subprocess.Popen[bytes]) -> bytes:
+    """Stop a child the test started; returns its output."""
+    if p.poll() is None:
+        p.terminate()
+        try:
+            p.wait(timeout=10)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            p.kill()
+            p.wait(timeout=10)
+    if p.stdout is None or p.stdout.closed:  # stopping twice (as test_crash_d2_subprocess does) is harmless
+        return b""
+    out = p.stdout.read()
+    p.stdout.close()
+    return out
+
+
+def is_write(fn: Any, name: str) -> bool:
+    """True when `fn` (a function handed to `Desk._locked_retry`) belongs to the method or inner function called
+    `name`. Whole dotted parts are compared, never a substring, and a test that selects a fault this way must also
+    assert that the fault fired (a rename would otherwise turn the test into a silent no-op)."""
+    return name in fn.__qualname__.split(".")
+
+
+def lock_writes_after_answer(rig: Any, qualifier: Any, monkeypatch: Any, where: str) -> None:
+    """Make the real write path (`Desk._write`, behind the real `_locked_retry`) refuse with a busy error for the one
+    write named by `where` ("_touch" or "store") once `qualifier.answered` is set."""
+    real = rig.desk._write
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def write(conn: Any) -> Iterator[None]:
+        caller = sys._getframe(2).f_code.co_qualname  # frame 1 is contextlib's __enter__; 2 is the writing function
+        if qualifier.answered and where in caller:
+            raise sqlite3.OperationalError("database is locked")
+        with real(conn):
+            yield
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rig.desk, "_write", write)
+
+
+def stall_report(rig: Rig) -> str:
+    """What the desk looks like when a wait for the follow-ups ran out: row states, the oldest pending rows, the
+    adapter worker counts, the reaper and the drive places. Read-only; used in the failure message."""
+    d = rig.desk
+    by_state = rig.query("SELECT state, last_error, count(*) FROM followups GROUP BY 1, 2")
+    oldest = rig.query(
+        "SELECT lead_id, state, auto_attempts, last_error, updated_at FROM followups WHERE state != 'sent'"
+        " ORDER BY updated_at LIMIT 5"
+    )
+    free = getattr(d._drives, "_free", None)  # noqa: SLF001

+def wait_until(fn: Callable[[], Any], timeout: float = WAIT_SECONDS, what: str = "condition") -> Any:
+    """Bounded poll. Returns the first truthy value of fn(); raises AssertionError after the timeout."""
+    end = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while True:

+class Clock:
+    def __init__(self, start: int = 1_700_000_000) -> None:

+    def advance(self, seconds: int) -> None:

+MIN_FAKE_STEP = 1e-6  # seconds a fake sleep always advances the clock

+class FakeClock:
+    """time.monotonic and time.sleep for the module under test: sleeping moves the clock, nothing really waits."""
+
+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:  # a pytest MonkeyPatch
+        self.now = 1000.0
+        self.sleeps: list[float] = []
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "monotonic", lambda: self.now)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", self._sleep)

+    def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:
+        # A sleep always moves the clock by a visible step: a wait of 1e-13 added to 1030.0 changes nothing in a
+        # float, and a retry loop whose `left` never reaches 0 then never ends. The cap on
+        # the list makes such a loop fail loudly instead.
+        assert len(self.sleeps) < MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS, "the loop under test never ends"

+class CrashAt(Hooks):

+        if name in self.points and name not in self.fired:

+class CountingCrm:
+    """An in-process CRM that tells a double put apart from a harmless repeat. capability "keyed": a second put with
+    the same lead id is ALREADY_PRESENT and stores nothing. "blind": it cannot tell, so EVERY put stores one more
+    row. `calls` is the log of every put (lead id, record); `rows` the stored ones, so a double put on either kind
+    shows as len(rows) == 2 (blind) or len(calls) > the allowed number (keyed)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mode: str = "keyed") -> None:
+        if mode not in ("keyed", "blind"):
+            raise ValueError(mode)
+        self.capability = mode
+        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        self.rows: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        # every set_fields call (lead id, email key, CRM owner id, CRM status); kept apart from `calls` because tests
+        # assert on the number of puts there
+        self.set_fields_calls: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()

+    @property
+    def count(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.rows)

+    def put(self, lead_id: str, record: Any) -> str:
+        with self._lock:
+            self.calls.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            if self.capability == "keyed" and any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                return "ALREADY_PRESENT"
+            self.rows.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            return "PUT"

+    def set_fields(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str, crm_owner_id: str, crm_status: str) -> None:
+        """Logs into set_fields_calls only; a lead with no stored put has no contact (as FakeCrm and HubSpot)."""
+        with self._lock:

+    def state(self, lead_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:

+    def restart(self, hooks: Hooks | None = None) -> Desk:

+        try:

+def rows(db_path: Path, sql: str, args: tuple[Any, ...] = ()) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:

+    crm_kind: str | None = None,

+) -> Rig:
+    """Config on tmp_path, in-process fakes, a Desk (started unless start=False). `leadflow` (a dict shaped like the
+    leadflow file, for example a deepcopy of DEMO_LEADFLOW) turns the lead owner, lead stage and reminder feature
+    on: it is written to tmp_path and read back by the real parser, so a test can never build a Leadflow the desk

+def addr(base: str) -> tuple[str, int]:

+def raw_http(base: str, request_bytes: bytes, timeout: float = 10.0) -> bytes:
+    """Send raw bytes on a socket and read until the server ends the connection. A reset after some bytes arrived (the
+    server closed with unread request bytes, as it does for an oversize body) ends the read: what came is returned."""
+    chunks: list[bytes] = []
+    with socket.create_connection(addr(base), timeout=timeout) as s:

+            s.sendall(request_bytes)
+        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):  # the server already answered and closed

+        except ConnectionResetError:

+    """Run each fn in its own thread behind one start barrier. Returns results (or the exception object) in order."""
+    barrier = threading.Barrier(len(fns))
+    out: list[Any] = [None] * len(fns)
+
+    def wrap(i: int) -> None:
+        barrier.wait()
+        try:
+            out[i] = fns[i]()
+        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (collected and returned to the caller)

+    """Serves GET /fake/info normally; POST /fake/outbox does what `behaviour` says."""

+    def __init__(self, behaviour: str, status: int = 200, body: bytes = b"{}") -> None:

+            def _json(self, status_: int, raw: bytes) -> None:

+            def do_GET(self) -> None:

+def is_write(fn: Any, name: str) -> bool:
+    """True when `fn` (a function handed to `Desk._locked_retry`) belongs to the method or inner function called

+    """An in-process CRM that tells a double put apart from a harmless repeat. capability "keyed": a second put with

+    row. `calls` is the log of every put (lead id, record); `rows` the stored ones, so a double put on either kind

+    """Send raw bytes on a socket and read until the server ends the connection. A reset after some bytes arrived (the
+    server closed with unread request bytes, as it does for an oversize body) ends the read: what came is returned."""
+    chunks: list[bytes] = []

+ENV_NAMES = {
+    "env",
+    "environ",
+    "config_env",
+    "os_environ",

+CASTS = {"int", "float", "Decimal"}
+SANITIZERS = {

+    "number",
+    "positive_seconds",
+}  # these return a checked number: not environment text any more
+LOADERS = {"load_env", "getenv"}  # calls whose result is settings text
+ENV_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*_[A-Z0-9_]+")  # a literal key such as "DESK_PORT" marks a settings mapping

+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """A direct-only scan (the contrast for the full one): a cast whose own argument
+    mentions an env name, a Subscript/Call on one, or `.environ` / `getenv`."""
+    hits = []
+    for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id in CASTS and n.args:
+            for m in ast.walk(n.args[0]):
+                if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript | ast.Call):
+                    base = m.value if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) else getattr(m.func, "value", None)
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Name) and base.id in ENV_NAMES:
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Attribute) and base.attr == "environ":
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+    return hits
+
+
+def _is_cast_expr(node: ast.AST, aliases: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """int, float, Decimal, decimal.Decimal, builtins.int, an alias of one, or functools.partial(<one of these>)."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
+        return node.id in CASTS or node.id in aliases
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
+        return node.attr in CASTS
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
+        fn = node.func
+        is_partial = (isinstance(fn, ast.Name) and fn.id == "partial") or (
+            isinstance(fn, ast.Attribute) and fn.attr == "partial"
+        )
+        return is_partial and bool(node.args) and _is_cast_expr(node.args[0], aliases)
+    return False
+
+
+def _cast_aliases(tree: ast.AST) -> set[str]:
+    """Names that stand for a number cast: `_i = int`, `conv = functools.partial(int)`, `from decimal import Decimal
+    as D`, `from builtins import int as I`."""
+    aliases: set[str] = set()
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for n in ast.walk(tree):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module in ("decimal", "builtins"):
+                for a in n.names:
+                    if a.name in CASTS and (a.asname or a.name) not in aliases and a.asname:
+                        aliases.add(a.asname)
+                        changed = True
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and _is_cast_expr(n.value, aliases):
+                for tgt in n.targets:
+                    if isinstance(tgt, ast.Name) and tgt.id not in aliases:
+                        aliases.add(tgt.id)
+                        changed = True
+    return aliases
+
+
+def _scopes(tree: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The module and every function."""
+    return [tree, *[n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)]]
+
+
+def _walk_scope(scope: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """Every node of a scope; the module scope leaves out the function bodies (they are scopes of their own)."""
+    if not isinstance(scope, ast.Module):
+        return list(ast.walk(scope))
+    out: list[ast.AST] = []
+    stack: list[ast.AST] = [scope]
+    while stack:
+        n = stack.pop()
+        out.append(n)
+        stack.extend(c for c in ast.iter_child_nodes(n) if not isinstance(c, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
+    return out

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the scan: no bare number cast on environment text
+ENV_NAMES = {
+    "env",
+    "environ",
+    "config_env",
+    "os_environ",
+}  # plus any parameter typed Mapping[str, str] or dict[str, str]
+CASTS = {"int", "float", "Decimal"}
+SANITIZERS = {
+    "env_number",
+    "number",
+    "positive_seconds",
+}  # these return a checked number: not environment text any more
+LOADERS = {"load_env", "getenv"}  # calls whose result is settings text
+ENV_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*_[A-Z0-9_]+")  # a literal key such as "DESK_PORT" marks a settings mapping
+SCAN_FOLDERS = ("src", "scripts", "demo_only", "load_tools", "tools")
+
+
+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """A direct-only scan (the contrast for the full one): a cast whose own argument
+    mentions an env name, a Subscript/Call on one, or `.environ` / `getenv`."""
+    hits = []
+    for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id in CASTS and n.args:
+            for m in ast.walk(n.args[0]):
+                if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript | ast.Call):
+                    base = m.value if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) else getattr(m.func, "value", None)
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Name) and base.id in ENV_NAMES:
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Attribute) and base.attr == "environ":
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+    return hits
+
+
+def _is_cast_expr(node: ast.AST, aliases: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """int, float, Decimal, decimal.Decimal, builtins.int, an alias of one, or functools.partial(<one of these>)."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
+        return node.id in CASTS or node.id in aliases
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
+        return node.attr in CASTS
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
+        fn = node.func
+        is_partial = (isinstance(fn, ast.Name) and fn.id == "partial") or (
+            isinstance(fn, ast.Attribute) and fn.attr == "partial"
+        )
+        return is_partial and bool(node.args) and _is_cast_expr(node.args[0], aliases)
+    return False
+
+
+def _cast_aliases(tree: ast.AST) -> set[str]:
+    """Names that stand for a number cast: `_i = int`, `conv = functools.partial(int)`, `from decimal import Decimal
+    as D`, `from builtins import int as I`."""
+    aliases: set[str] = set()
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for n in ast.walk(tree):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module in ("decimal", "builtins"):
+                for a in n.names:
+                    if a.name in CASTS and (a.asname or a.name) not in aliases and a.asname:
+                        aliases.add(a.asname)
+                        changed = True
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and _is_cast_expr(n.value, aliases):
+                for tgt in n.targets:
+                    if isinstance(tgt, ast.Name) and tgt.id not in aliases:
+                        aliases.add(tgt.id)
+                        changed = True
+    return aliases
+
+
+def _scopes(tree: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The module and every function."""
+    return [tree, *[n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)]]
+
+
+def _walk_scope(scope: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """Every node of a scope; the module scope leaves out the function bodies (they are scopes of their own)."""
+    if not isinstance(scope, ast.Module):
+        return list(ast.walk(scope))
+    out: list[ast.AST] = []
+    stack: list[ast.AST] = [scope]
+    while stack:
+        n = stack.pop()
+        out.append(n)
+        stack.extend(c for c in ast.iter_child_nodes(n) if not isinstance(c, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
+    return out
+
+
+def _touches(node: ast.AST, tainted: set[str], attrs: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """Does this expression hold settings text? A tainted name, `.environ`/`getenv`, an attribute that was assigned
+    settings text somewhere in the file (`self.raw`), a call of a loader, or a subscript / `.get` with a literal key
+    that looks like a setting name (`cfg["DESK_PORT"]`), whatever the mapping is called."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id in SANITIZERS:
+        return False  # a checked number is not environment text any more
+    for m in ast.walk(node):
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Name) and m.id in tainted:
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Attribute) and (m.attr in ("environ", "getenv", "environb") or m.attr in attrs):
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Call):
+            name = m.func.id if isinstance(m.func, ast.Name) else getattr(m.func, "attr", "")
+            if name in LOADERS:
+                return True
+            if name == "get" and m.args and isinstance(m.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(m.args[0].value, str):
+                if ENV_KEY.fullmatch(m.args[0].value):
+                    return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) and isinstance(m.slice, ast.Constant) and isinstance(m.slice.value, str):
+            if ENV_KEY.fullmatch(m.slice.value):
+                return True
+    return False
+
+
+def _bound(target: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The names and attributes an assignment target binds (a store into `x[k]` binds neither)."""
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Name | ast.Attribute):
+        return [target]
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Tuple | ast.List):
+        return [b for el in target.elts for b in _bound(el)]
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Starred):
+        return _bound(target.value)
+    return []
+
+
+def _analyse(tree: ast.AST) -> tuple[dict[int, set[str]], set[str]]:
+    """Names (per scope) and attributes that hold settings text. Module-level taint is visible in every function; an
+    attribute assigned settings text anywhere in the file (`self.raw = ...`) is tainted wherever it is read."""
+    imported: set[str] = set()
+    for n in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module == "os":
+            imported.update(a.asname or a.name for a in n.names if a.name in ("environ", "getenv", "environb"))
+    scopes = _scopes(tree)
+    by_scope: dict[int, set[str]] = {id(s): set(ENV_NAMES) | imported for s in scopes}
+    attrs: set[str] = set()
+    for s in scopes:
+        if isinstance(s, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
+            for arg in (*s.args.posonlyargs, *s.args.args, *s.args.kwonlyargs):
+                if arg.annotation is not None and ast.unparse(arg.annotation).startswith(
+                    ("Mapping[str, str]", "dict[str, str]")
+                ):
+                    by_scope[id(s)].add(arg.arg)  # def f(e: Mapping[str, str]): e is a settings mapping
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for s in scopes:
+            cur = by_scope[id(s)]
+            if s is not tree:

+            return True
+        time.sleep(0.02)
+    return condition()

+def fail_until_the_cap(rig: Rig, lid: str, mode: str, err: str) -> None:

+    unclear send is tried again by the reaper after 1, 2, 4, 8 s). Make every further try fail the same way until
+    the cap of SEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS tries in all; only then is it `failed`."""

+    for _ in range(SEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1):
+        rig.outbox.fail_next(mode)
+        rig.clock.advance(20)  # longer than the longest wait between tries
+        rig.desk.reap_once()
+    assert rig.state(lid) == ("failed", err)

+            self.hang_refresh = False
+            self.entered: list[str] = []
+            self.refreshes = 0
+            self._hung: set[str] = set()

Lambda may not be necessary


A lambda that calls a function without modifying any of its parameters is unnecessary. Python functions are first-class objects and can be passed around in the same way as the resulting lambda. It is recommended to remove the lambda and use the function directly.

+def test_workers_stay_within_the_cap(env, monkeypatch) -> None:
+    """8 drives ask the model at the same moment: at most the cap of workers is ever started (the slot is taken
+    before the worker starts; a check that only reads a count raised later lets all 8 through)."""
+    rig = env.rig()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(desk_module, "MODEL_CALL_BUDGET_SECONDS", SHORT)
+    started = 0
+    gate_open = threading.Event()
+    lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    class Counted(RecordedQualifier):
+        def qualify(self, lead_id: str, email_key: str) -> Any:
+            nonlocal started
+            with lock:
+                started += 1
+            gate_open.wait(8)
+            return "warm"
+
+    rig.desk.qualifier = Counted(rig.replies_path)
+    parties = 8
+    start = threading.Barrier(parties, timeout=15)
+    outcomes: list[str] = []
+
+    def one() -> None:
+        start.wait()
+        try:
+            rig.desk._ask_model("L0", "a@example.test")
+            outcomes.append("answered")
+        except ModelBusy:
+            outcomes.append("busy")
+        except ModelTimeout:
+            outcomes.append("timeout")
+
+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=one) for _ in range(parties)]
+    for t in threads:
+        t.start()
+    for t in threads:
+        t.join(15)
+    try:
+        assert not any(t.is_alive() for t in threads)
+        assert started == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert sorted(outcomes) == ["busy"] * (parties - gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX) + ["timeout"] * gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+        assert rig.desk.hung_workers()["model"] == gate.MODEL_HUNG_MAX
+    finally:
+        gate_open.set()
+    assert wait_for(lambda: drained(rig))
+

+def wait_until(fn: Callable[[], Any], timeout: float = WAIT_SECONDS, what: str = "condition") -> Any:

+    while True:

+    def __init__(self, start: int = 1_700_000_000) -> None:

+    def __call__(self) -> int:

+
+    def advance(self, seconds: int) -> None:
+        self.t += seconds

+MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS = 5000  # a loop on the fake clock that sleeps more often than this is stuck
+MIN_FAKE_STEP = 1e-6  # seconds a fake sleep always advances the clock

+class FakeClock:
+    """time.monotonic and time.sleep for the module under test: sleeping moves the clock, nothing really waits."""
+
+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:  # a pytest MonkeyPatch
+        self.now = 1000.0
+        self.sleeps: list[float] = []
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "monotonic", lambda: self.now)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", self._sleep)

+    def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:
+        # A sleep always moves the clock by a visible step: a wait of 1e-13 added to 1030.0 changes nothing in a
+        # float, and a retry loop whose `left` never reaches 0 then never ends. The cap on
+        # the list makes such a loop fail loudly instead.
+        assert len(self.sleeps) < MAX_FAKE_SLEEPS, "the loop under test never ends"

+    passed the row's wait, so a frozen Clock would leave every row the request's own drive gave back for ever."""

+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__(int(time.time()))  # wall-clock: the desk's own calendar stamps

+class CrashAt(Hooks):

+    as a kill would."""

+        self.points = set(points)
+        self.fired: list[str] = []

+        if name in self.points and name not in self.fired:
+            self.fired.append(name)
+            if conn is not None and conn.in_transaction:
+                conn.rollback()

+class BlockAt(Hooks):
+    """Block once at `point` until release is set (holds a receipt open, or a follow-up in `sending`)."""

+        self.reached = threading.Event()
+        self.release = threading.Event()

+            self.release.wait(timeout=WAIT_SECONDS)

+class CountingCrm:
+    """An in-process CRM that tells a double put apart from a harmless repeat. capability "keyed": a second put with
+    the same lead id is ALREADY_PRESENT and stores nothing. "blind": it cannot tell, so EVERY put stores one more
+    row. `calls` is the log of every put (lead id, record); `rows` the stored ones, so a double put on either kind
+    shows as len(rows) == 2 (blind) or len(calls) > the allowed number (keyed)."""

+    def __init__(self, mode: str = "keyed") -> None:

+            raise ValueError(mode)

+        self.rows: list[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]] = []
+        # every set_fields call (lead id, email key, CRM owner id, CRM status); kept apart from `calls` because tests
+        # assert on the number of puts there
+        self.set_fields_calls: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()

+    @property
+    def count(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.rows)

+    def put(self, lead_id: str, record: Any) -> str:
+        with self._lock:
+            self.calls.append((lead_id, dict(record)))
+            if self.capability == "keyed" and any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):
+                return "ALREADY_PRESENT"

+            self.set_fields_calls.append((lead_id, email_key, crm_owner_id, crm_status))
+            if not any(k == lead_id for k, _ in self.rows):

+# -- desk builder
+@dataclass
+class Rig:

+    config: Config

+    outbox: Any
+    qualifier: RecordedQualifier

+    db_path: Path
+    replies_path: Path
+    desks: list[Desk] = field(default_factory=list)

+    def query(self, sql: str, args: tuple[Any, ...] = ()) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:

+    def leads(self) -> int:

+    def state(self, lead_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
+        sql = "SELECT state, last_error FROM followups" + (" WHERE lead_id=?" if lead_id else "")  # noqa: S608
+        r = self.query(sql, (lead_id,) if lead_id else ())

+    def restart(self, hooks: Hooks | None = None) -> Desk:
+        """A new Desk on the same lead book and the same fakes, then startup() (the sweep). The old one is closed."""
+        try:
+            self.desk.close()
+        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001, S110 (a crashed desk may fail to close; the file is what matters)

+        self.desk = Desk(

+def rows(db_path: Path, sql: str, args: tuple[Any, ...] = ()) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:

+    leadflow: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
+    outbox_kind: str | None = None,
+    crm_kind: str | None = None,
+    **config_over: Any,
+) -> Rig:
+    """Config on tmp_path, in-process fakes, a Desk (started unless start=False). `leadflow` (a dict shaped like the
+    leadflow file, for example a deepcopy of DEMO_LEADFLOW) turns the lead owner, lead stage and reminder feature
+    on: it is written to tmp_path and read back by the real parser, so a test can never build a Leadflow the desk
+    would refuse. None (the default) leaves the feature off."""

+        config_over["crm"] = crm_kind

+    """Send raw bytes on a socket and read until the server ends the connection. A reset after some bytes arrived (the
+    server closed with unread request bytes, as it does for an oversize body) ends the read: what came is returned."""
+    chunks: list[bytes] = []
+    with socket.create_connection(addr(base), timeout=timeout) as s:

+            s.sendall(request_bytes)
+        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):  # the server already answered and closed

+# -- a tiny stand-in sender with scripted misbehaviour (for test_error_mapping)
+class StubSender:
+    """Serves GET /fake/info normally; POST /fake/outbox does what `behaviour` says."""

+    def __init__(self, behaviour: str, status: int = 200, body: bytes = b"{}") -> None:

+            def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None:  # noqa: A002

+            def do_GET(self) -> None:

+        self.thread.start()
+        self.url = f"http://{HOST}:{self.srv.server_address[1]}"

+        self.srv.shutdown()

+# -- subprocess helpers
+def start_proc(args: list[str], env: dict[str, str]) -> subprocess.Popen[bytes]:

+def stop_proc(p: subprocess.Popen[bytes]) -> bytes:

+    if p.poll() is None:

+        try:
+            p.wait(timeout=10)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:

+            p.wait(timeout=10)

+def is_write(fn: Any, name: str) -> bool:
+    """True when `fn` (a function handed to `Desk._locked_retry`) belongs to the method or inner function called
+    `name`. Whole dotted parts are compared, never a substring, and a test that selects a fault this way must also
+    assert that the fault fired (a rename would otherwise turn the test into a silent no-op)."""
+    return name in fn.__qualname__.split(".")

+def lock_writes_after_answer(rig: Any, qualifier: Any, monkeypatch: Any, where: str) -> None:
+    """Make the real write path (`Desk._write`, behind the real `_locked_retry`) refuse with a busy error for the one

+        if qualifier.answered and where in caller:
+            raise sqlite3.OperationalError("database is locked")

+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rig.desk, "_write", write)
+
+
+def stall_report(rig: Rig) -> str:
+    """What the desk looks like when a wait for the follow-ups ran out: row states, the oldest pending rows, the

+    d = rig.desk

+        "SELECT lead_id, state, auto_attempts, last_error, updated_at FROM followups WHERE state != 'sent'"
+        " ORDER BY updated_at LIMIT 5"
+    )
+    free = getattr(d._drives, "_free", None)  # noqa: SLF001

+        config_over["leadflow"] = lf
+        config_over.setdefault("nudge_to", NUDGE_TO_TEST if lf.nudge_after_seconds is not None else "")
+    config = Config(db_path=tmp_path / "desk.sqlite3", port=0, replies_path=replies_path, **config_over)
+    ob = {"keyed": KeyedOutbox, "blind": BlindOutbox}[outbox]() if isinstance(outbox, str) else outbox
+    crm, qual, clock = crm or FakeCrm(), RecordedQualifier(replies_path), clock or Clock()
+    desk = Desk(config, crm, ob, qual, hooks=hooks, now=clock, schema_sql=schema_sql)

+    if start:
+        desk.startup()
+    return rig
+

+# -- HTTP helpers
+_OPENER = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
+
+

+    data = raw if raw is not None else (None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode())
+    req = urllib.request.Request(base + path, data=data, method=method)  # noqa: S310 (loopback test URL)
+    if data is not None:
+        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
+    try:
+        with _OPENER.open(req, timeout=timeout) as r:  # noqa: S310

+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+        return e.code, json.loads(e.read().decode() or "null")
+
+

+    return call(base, "POST", "/leads", {"source": source, "source_ref": ref, "payload": payload})  # type: ignore[no-any-return]
+
+
+def addr(base: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
+    """(host, port) of a base URL such as http://127.0.0.1:8080."""
+    host, port = base.removeprefix("http://").split(":")
+    return host, int(port)
+
+
+def raw_http(base: str, request_bytes: bytes, timeout: float = 10.0) -> bytes:
+    """Send raw bytes on a socket and read until the server ends the connection. A reset after some bytes arrived (the
+    server closed with unread request bytes, as it does for an oversize body) ends the read: what came is returned."""
+    chunks: list[bytes] = []
+    with socket.create_connection(addr(base), timeout=timeout) as s:
+        try:
+            s.sendall(request_bytes)
+        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):  # the server already answered and closed
+            pass
+        try:
+            while chunk := s.recv(65536):
+                chunks.append(chunk)
+        except ConnectionResetError:
+            pass
+    return b"".join(chunks)
+
+
+def raw_exchange(base: str, request_bytes: bytes, timeout: float = 10.0) -> tuple[int, Any]:
+    """Send raw bytes on a socket, read to the end of the connection, return (status, JSON body)."""
+    data = raw_http(base, request_bytes, timeout)
+    head, _, body = data.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
+    status = int(head.split(b" ", 2)[1])
+    return status, json.loads(body.decode() or "null")

+    """Run each fn in its own thread behind one start barrier. Returns results (or the exception object) in order."""
+    barrier = threading.Barrier(len(fns))
+    out: list[Any] = [None] * len(fns)
+
+    def wrap(i: int) -> None:
+        barrier.wait()
+        try:
+            out[i] = fns[i]()
+        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (collected and returned to the caller)
+            out[i] = e
+
+    ts = [threading.Thread(target=wrap, args=(i,)) for i in range(len(fns))]

+class StubSender:
+    """Serves GET /fake/info normally; POST /fake/outbox does what `behaviour` says."""

+    def __init__(self, behaviour: str, status: int = 200, body: bytes = b"{}") -> None:

+        class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):

+
+            def _json(self, status_: int, raw: bytes) -> None:

+                    return None
+                if outer.behaviour == "garbage":

+        self.url = f"http://{HOST}:{self.srv.server_address[1]}"
+

+        self.srv.shutdown()
+        self.srv.server_close()
+        self.thread.join(timeout=5)

+    return subprocess.Popen(  # noqa: S603 (this repository's interpreter and modules)
+        [sys.executable, *args], cwd=REPO, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT
+    )
+

+    """Stop a child the test started; returns its output."""
+    if p.poll() is None:

+        try:
+            p.wait(timeout=10)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            p.kill()

+    if p.stdout is None or p.stdout.closed:  # stopping twice (as test_crash_d2_subprocess does) is harmless

+def is_write(fn: Any, name: str) -> bool:
+    """True when `fn` (a function handed to `Desk._locked_retry`) belongs to the method or inner function called
+    `name`. Whole dotted parts are compared, never a substring, and a test that selects a fault this way must also
+    assert that the fault fired (a rename would otherwise turn the test into a silent no-op)."""

+    """Make the real write path (`Desk._write`, behind the real `_locked_retry`) refuse with a busy error for the one
+    write named by `where` ("_touch" or "store") once `qualifier.answered` is set."""
+    real = rig.desk._write

+    @contextmanager
+    def write(conn: Any) -> Iterator[None]:
+        caller = sys._getframe(2).f_code.co_qualname  # frame 1 is contextlib's __enter__; 2 is the writing function

+        with real(conn):

+    monkeypatch.setattr(rig.desk, "_write", write)

+def stall_report(rig: Rig) -> str:
+    """What the desk looks like when a wait for the follow-ups ran out: row states, the oldest pending rows, the
+    adapter worker counts, the reaper and the drive places. Read-only; used in the failure message."""
+    d = rig.desk
+    by_state = rig.query("SELECT state, last_error, count(*) FROM followups GROUP BY 1, 2")
+    oldest = rig.query(
+        "SELECT lead_id, state, auto_attempts, last_error, updated_at FROM followups WHERE state != 'sent'"
+        " ORDER BY updated_at LIMIT 5"
+    )
+    free = getattr(d._drives, "_free", None)  # noqa: SLF001
+    waiting = len(getattr(d._drives, "_waiters", ()))  # noqa: SLF001
+    return (
+        f"states={by_state}\noldest={oldest}\nnow={d._now()} workers={dict(d._workers)} "  # noqa: SLF001
+        f"abandoned={dict(d._abandoned)}\nreaper_running={d.reaper_running()} drive_free={free} "  # noqa: SLF001

Access to a protected member _abandoned of a client class


Accessing a protected member (a member prefixed with `_`) of a class from outside that class is not recommended, since the creator of that class did not intend this member to be exposed. If accesing this attribute outside of the class is absolutely needed, refactor it such that it becomes part of the public interface of the class.

+def hold_write_lock(db_path: Path, seconds: float) -> Callable[[], None]:
+    """Another writer: BEGIN IMMEDIATE on its own connection, released after `seconds` (or at once by the returned
+    function, which the test calls in a finally block so no lock outlives its test). The timer is a daemon."""

'subprocess.run' used without explicitly defining the value for 'check'.


`subprocess.run` uses a default of `check=False`, which means that a nonzero exit code will be ignored by default, instead of raising an exception. You can ignore this issue if this behaviour is intended.

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the scan: no bare number cast on environment text
+ENV_NAMES = {
+    "env",
+    "environ",
+    "config_env",
+    "os_environ",
+}  # plus any parameter typed Mapping[str, str] or dict[str, str]
+CASTS = {"int", "float", "Decimal"}
+SANITIZERS = {
+    "env_number",
+    "number",
+    "positive_seconds",
+}  # these return a checked number: not environment text any more
+LOADERS = {"load_env", "getenv"}  # calls whose result is settings text
+ENV_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*_[A-Z0-9_]+")  # a literal key such as "DESK_PORT" marks a settings mapping
+SCAN_FOLDERS = ("src", "scripts", "demo_only", "load_tools", "tools")
+
+
+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """A direct-only scan (the contrast for the full one): a cast whose own argument
+    mentions an env name, a Subscript/Call on one, or `.environ` / `getenv`."""
+    hits = []
+    for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id in CASTS and n.args:
+            for m in ast.walk(n.args[0]):
+                if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript | ast.Call):
+                    base = m.value if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) else getattr(m.func, "value", None)
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Name) and base.id in ENV_NAMES:
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Attribute) and base.attr == "environ":
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+    return hits
+
+
+def _is_cast_expr(node: ast.AST, aliases: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """int, float, Decimal, decimal.Decimal, builtins.int, an alias of one, or functools.partial(<one of these>)."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
+        return node.id in CASTS or node.id in aliases
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
+        return node.attr in CASTS
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
+        fn = node.func
+        is_partial = (isinstance(fn, ast.Name) and fn.id == "partial") or (
+            isinstance(fn, ast.Attribute) and fn.attr == "partial"
+        )
+        return is_partial and bool(node.args) and _is_cast_expr(node.args[0], aliases)
+    return False
+
+
+def _cast_aliases(tree: ast.AST) -> set[str]:
+    """Names that stand for a number cast: `_i = int`, `conv = functools.partial(int)`, `from decimal import Decimal
+    as D`, `from builtins import int as I`."""
+    aliases: set[str] = set()
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for n in ast.walk(tree):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module in ("decimal", "builtins"):
+                for a in n.names:
+                    if a.name in CASTS and (a.asname or a.name) not in aliases and a.asname:
+                        aliases.add(a.asname)
+                        changed = True
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and _is_cast_expr(n.value, aliases):
+                for tgt in n.targets:
+                    if isinstance(tgt, ast.Name) and tgt.id not in aliases:
+                        aliases.add(tgt.id)
+                        changed = True
+    return aliases
+
+
+def _scopes(tree: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The module and every function."""
+    return [tree, *[n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)]]
+
+
+def _walk_scope(scope: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """Every node of a scope; the module scope leaves out the function bodies (they are scopes of their own)."""
+    if not isinstance(scope, ast.Module):
+        return list(ast.walk(scope))
+    out: list[ast.AST] = []
+    stack: list[ast.AST] = [scope]
+    while stack:
+        n = stack.pop()
+        out.append(n)
+        stack.extend(c for c in ast.iter_child_nodes(n) if not isinstance(c, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
+    return out
+
+
+def _touches(node: ast.AST, tainted: set[str], attrs: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """Does this expression hold settings text? A tainted name, `.environ`/`getenv`, an attribute that was assigned
+    settings text somewhere in the file (`self.raw`), a call of a loader, or a subscript / `.get` with a literal key
+    that looks like a setting name (`cfg["DESK_PORT"]`), whatever the mapping is called."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id in SANITIZERS:
+        return False  # a checked number is not environment text any more
+    for m in ast.walk(node):
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Name) and m.id in tainted:
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Attribute) and (m.attr in ("environ", "getenv", "environb") or m.attr in attrs):
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Call):
+            name = m.func.id if isinstance(m.func, ast.Name) else getattr(m.func, "attr", "")
+            if name in LOADERS:
+                return True
+            if name == "get" and m.args and isinstance(m.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(m.args[0].value, str):
+                if ENV_KEY.fullmatch(m.args[0].value):
+                    return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) and isinstance(m.slice, ast.Constant) and isinstance(m.slice.value, str):
+            if ENV_KEY.fullmatch(m.slice.value):
+                return True
+    return False
+
+
+def _bound(target: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The names and attributes an assignment target binds (a store into `x[k]` binds neither)."""
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Name | ast.Attribute):
+        return [target]
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Tuple | ast.List):
+        return [b for el in target.elts for b in _bound(el)]
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Starred):
+        return _bound(target.value)
+    return []
+
+
+def _analyse(tree: ast.AST) -> tuple[dict[int, set[str]], set[str]]:
+    """Names (per scope) and attributes that hold settings text. Module-level taint is visible in every function; an
+    attribute assigned settings text anywhere in the file (`self.raw = ...`) is tainted wherever it is read."""
+    imported: set[str] = set()
+    for n in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module == "os":
+            imported.update(a.asname or a.name for a in n.names if a.name in ("environ", "getenv", "environb"))
+    scopes = _scopes(tree)
+    by_scope: dict[int, set[str]] = {id(s): set(ENV_NAMES) | imported for s in scopes}
+    attrs: set[str] = set()
+    for s in scopes:
+        if isinstance(s, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
+            for arg in (*s.args.posonlyargs, *s.args.args, *s.args.kwonlyargs):
+                if arg.annotation is not None and ast.unparse(arg.annotation).startswith(
+                    ("Mapping[str, str]", "dict[str, str]")
+                ):
+                    by_scope[id(s)].add(arg.arg)  # def f(e: Mapping[str, str]): e is a settings mapping
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for s in scopes:
+            cur = by_scope[id(s)]
+            if s is not tree:
+                cur |= by_scope[id(tree)]  # module-level taint reaches the functions
+            for n in _walk_scope(s):
+                targets: list[ast.expr] = []
+                value: ast.AST | None = None
+                if isinstance(n, ast.Assign):

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the scan: no bare number cast on environment text
+ENV_NAMES = {
+    "env",
+    "environ",
+    "config_env",
+    "os_environ",
+}  # plus any parameter typed Mapping[str, str] or dict[str, str]
+CASTS = {"int", "float", "Decimal"}
+SANITIZERS = {
+    "env_number",
+    "number",
+    "positive_seconds",
+}  # these return a checked number: not environment text any more
+LOADERS = {"load_env", "getenv"}  # calls whose result is settings text
+ENV_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*_[A-Z0-9_]+")  # a literal key such as "DESK_PORT" marks a settings mapping
+SCAN_FOLDERS = ("src", "scripts", "demo_only", "load_tools", "tools")
+
+
+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """A direct-only scan (the contrast for the full one): a cast whose own argument
+    mentions an env name, a Subscript/Call on one, or `.environ` / `getenv`."""
+    hits = []
+    for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id in CASTS and n.args:
+            for m in ast.walk(n.args[0]):
+                if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript | ast.Call):
+                    base = m.value if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) else getattr(m.func, "value", None)
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Name) and base.id in ENV_NAMES:
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Attribute) and base.attr == "environ":
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+    return hits
+
+
+def _is_cast_expr(node: ast.AST, aliases: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """int, float, Decimal, decimal.Decimal, builtins.int, an alias of one, or functools.partial(<one of these>)."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
+        return node.id in CASTS or node.id in aliases
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
+        return node.attr in CASTS
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
+        fn = node.func
+        is_partial = (isinstance(fn, ast.Name) and fn.id == "partial") or (
+            isinstance(fn, ast.Attribute) and fn.attr == "partial"
+        )
+        return is_partial and bool(node.args) and _is_cast_expr(node.args[0], aliases)
+    return False
+
+
+def _cast_aliases(tree: ast.AST) -> set[str]:
+    """Names that stand for a number cast: `_i = int`, `conv = functools.partial(int)`, `from decimal import Decimal
+    as D`, `from builtins import int as I`."""
+    aliases: set[str] = set()
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for n in ast.walk(tree):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module in ("decimal", "builtins"):
+                for a in n.names:
+                    if a.name in CASTS and (a.asname or a.name) not in aliases and a.asname:
+                        aliases.add(a.asname)
+                        changed = True
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and _is_cast_expr(n.value, aliases):
+                for tgt in n.targets:
+                    if isinstance(tgt, ast.Name) and tgt.id not in aliases:
+                        aliases.add(tgt.id)
+                        changed = True
+    return aliases
+
+
+def _scopes(tree: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The module and every function."""
+    return [tree, *[n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)]]
+
+
+def _walk_scope(scope: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """Every node of a scope; the module scope leaves out the function bodies (they are scopes of their own)."""
+    if not isinstance(scope, ast.Module):
+        return list(ast.walk(scope))
+    out: list[ast.AST] = []
+    stack: list[ast.AST] = [scope]
+    while stack:
+        n = stack.pop()
+        out.append(n)
+        stack.extend(c for c in ast.iter_child_nodes(n) if not isinstance(c, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
+    return out
+
+
+def _touches(node: ast.AST, tainted: set[str], attrs: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """Does this expression hold settings text? A tainted name, `.environ`/`getenv`, an attribute that was assigned
+    settings text somewhere in the file (`self.raw`), a call of a loader, or a subscript / `.get` with a literal key
+    that looks like a setting name (`cfg["DESK_PORT"]`), whatever the mapping is called."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id in SANITIZERS:
+        return False  # a checked number is not environment text any more
+    for m in ast.walk(node):
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Name) and m.id in tainted:
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Attribute) and (m.attr in ("environ", "getenv", "environb") or m.attr in attrs):
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Call):
+            name = m.func.id if isinstance(m.func, ast.Name) else getattr(m.func, "attr", "")
+            if name in LOADERS:
+                return True
+            if name == "get" and m.args and isinstance(m.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(m.args[0].value, str):
+                if ENV_KEY.fullmatch(m.args[0].value):
+                    return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) and isinstance(m.slice, ast.Constant) and isinstance(m.slice.value, str):
+            if ENV_KEY.fullmatch(m.slice.value):
+                return True
+    return False
+
+
+def _bound(target: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The names and attributes an assignment target binds (a store into `x[k]` binds neither)."""
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Name | ast.Attribute):
+        return [target]
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Tuple | ast.List):
+        return [b for el in target.elts for b in _bound(el)]
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Starred):
+        return _bound(target.value)
+    return []
+
+
+def _analyse(tree: ast.AST) -> tuple[dict[int, set[str]], set[str]]:
+    """Names (per scope) and attributes that hold settings text. Module-level taint is visible in every function; an
+    attribute assigned settings text anywhere in the file (`self.raw = ...`) is tainted wherever it is read."""
+    imported: set[str] = set()
+    for n in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module == "os":
+            imported.update(a.asname or a.name for a in n.names if a.name in ("environ", "getenv", "environb"))
+    scopes = _scopes(tree)
+    by_scope: dict[int, set[str]] = {id(s): set(ENV_NAMES) | imported for s in scopes}
+    attrs: set[str] = set()
+    for s in scopes:
+        if isinstance(s, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
+            for arg in (*s.args.posonlyargs, *s.args.args, *s.args.kwonlyargs):
+                if arg.annotation is not None and ast.unparse(arg.annotation).startswith(
+                    ("Mapping[str, str]", "dict[str, str]")
+                ):
+                    by_scope[id(s)].add(arg.arg)  # def f(e: Mapping[str, str]): e is a settings mapping
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for s in scopes:
+            cur = by_scope[id(s)]
+            if s is not tree:
+                cur |= by_scope[id(tree)]  # module-level taint reaches the functions
+            for n in _walk_scope(s):
+                targets: list[ast.expr] = []
+                value: ast.AST | None = None
+                if isinstance(n, ast.Assign):
+                    targets, value = list(n.targets), n.value
+                elif isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign) and n.value is not None:
+                    targets, value = [n.target], n.value
+                elif isinstance(n, ast.NamedExpr | ast.AugAssign):
+                    targets, value = [n.target], n.value
+                elif isinstance(n, ast.For | ast.comprehension):
+                    targets, value = [n.target], n.iter
+                if value is None or not _touches(value, cur, attrs):
+                    continue
+                for tgt in targets:
+                    for node in _bound(tgt):
+                        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id not in cur:
+                            cur.add(node.id)
+                            changed = True
+                        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr not in attrs:
+                            attrs.add(node.attr)
+                            changed = True
+    return by_scope, attrs
+
+
+def _bare_casts(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """Lines where int(), float() or Decimal() (also under an alias, `decimal.Decimal`, `functools.partial`, `map`, or
+    as an argparse `type=`) is applied to settings text. COVERED: text read from `os.environ`, `os.getenv`, a name
+    imported from os, a parameter typed `Mapping[str, str]` or `dict[str, str]`, `load_env(...)`, or any mapping read with a literal key that
+    looks like a setting name; followed through assignments, loops, walrus, module-level names, and attributes such as
+    `self.raw`. NOT COVERED: taint that travels through a function's return value or through a container passed
+    between functions, a cast reached through getattr/eval, and numbers read from other files."""
+    tree = ast.parse(source)
+    aliases = _cast_aliases(tree)
+    by_scope, attrs = _analyse(tree)
+    hits: set[int] = set()
+    for scope in _scopes(tree):
+        tainted = by_scope[id(scope)]
+        for n in _walk_scope(scope):
+            if not isinstance(n, ast.Call):
+                continue
+            if _is_cast_expr(n.func, aliases) and any(_touches(a, tainted, attrs) for a in n.args):
+                hits.add(n.lineno)
+            if isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id == "map" and n.args and _is_cast_expr(n.args[0], aliases):
+                if any(_touches(a, tainted, attrs) for a in n.args[1:]):
+                    hits.add(n.lineno)
+            if isinstance(n.func, ast.Attribute) and n.func.attr == "add_argument":
+                kws = {k.arg: k.value for k in n.keywords}
+                kind = kws.get("type")
+                if kind is not None and _is_cast_expr(kind, aliases) and "default" in kws:
+                    if _touches(kws["default"], tainted, attrs):
+                        hits.add(n.lineno)
+    return sorted(hits)
+
+
+EVASIVE = {
+    "two step": 'raw = env.get("X")\nx = int(raw)',
+    "two step alias chain": 'raw = os.environ["X"]\nv = raw.strip()\nx = float(v)',
+    "decimal attribute": 'x = decimal.Decimal(env["X"])',

+        "updatedAt": "CANARY-updated",

+def _workflow_problems(text: str) -> list[str]:
+    """What is wrong with one workflow file: an Action not pinned by a full commit SHA, no top-level `permissions:`,
+    a write permission at the top level, or a trigger that hands secrets to code from a pull request."""
+    problems = [f"not pinned by full SHA: {u}" for u in USES_LINE.findall(text) if not PINNED.match(u)]
+    lines = text.splitlines()
+    top = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.startswith("permissions:")]
+    if len(top) != 1:
+        problems.append("needs exactly one top-level permissions: block")
+    else:
+        block = [lines[top[0]]]
+        for ln in lines[top[0] + 1 :]:
+            if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith((" ", "	", "#")):
+                break
+            block.append(ln)
+        if "write" in NL.join(block):
+            problems.append("top-level permissions must be read-only (raise per job)")
+    problems += [f"forbidden trigger: {t}" for t in FORBIDDEN_TRIGGERS if re.search(rf"^[ ]*{t}\b", text, re.MULTILINE)]

+ENV_NAMES = {
+    "env",
+    "environ",
+    "config_env",
+    "os_environ",

+CASTS = {"int", "float", "Decimal"}

+    "number",

+}  # these return a checked number: not environment text any more
+LOADERS = {"load_env", "getenv"}  # calls whose result is settings text
+ENV_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*_[A-Z0-9_]+")  # a literal key such as "DESK_PORT" marks a settings mapping

+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """A direct-only scan (the contrast for the full one): a cast whose own argument
+    mentions an env name, a Subscript/Call on one, or `.environ` / `getenv`."""
+    hits = []
+    for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id in CASTS and n.args:
+            for m in ast.walk(n.args[0]):
+                if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript | ast.Call):
+                    base = m.value if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) else getattr(m.func, "value", None)
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Name) and base.id in ENV_NAMES:
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Attribute) and base.attr == "environ":
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+    return hits
+

+def _is_cast_expr(node: ast.AST, aliases: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """int, float, Decimal, decimal.Decimal, builtins.int, an alias of one, or functools.partial(<one of these>)."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
+        return node.id in CASTS or node.id in aliases
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
+        return node.attr in CASTS
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):

+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """A direct-only scan (the contrast for the full one): a cast whose own argument
+    mentions an env name, a Subscript/Call on one, or `.environ` / `getenv`."""
+    hits = []
+    for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id in CASTS and n.args:
+            for m in ast.walk(n.args[0]):
+                if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript | ast.Call):
+                    base = m.value if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) else getattr(m.func, "value", None)
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Name) and base.id in ENV_NAMES:
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Attribute) and base.attr == "environ":
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)

+def _is_cast_expr(node: ast.AST, aliases: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """int, float, Decimal, decimal.Decimal, builtins.int, an alias of one, or functools.partial(<one of these>)."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
+        return node.id in CASTS or node.id in aliases
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
+        return node.attr in CASTS

+            isinstance(fn, ast.Attribute) and fn.attr == "partial"

+def _cast_aliases(tree: ast.AST) -> set[str]:

+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for n in ast.walk(tree):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module in ("decimal", "builtins"):
+                for a in n.names:
+                    if a.name in CASTS and (a.asname or a.name) not in aliases and a.asname:
+                        aliases.add(a.asname)
+                        changed = True
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and _is_cast_expr(n.value, aliases):
+                for tgt in n.targets:
+                    if isinstance(tgt, ast.Name) and tgt.id not in aliases:

+def _scopes(tree: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The module and every function."""
+    return [tree, *[n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)]]

+def _walk_scope(scope: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """Every node of a scope; the module scope leaves out the function bodies (they are scopes of their own)."""
+    if not isinstance(scope, ast.Module):
+        return list(ast.walk(scope))
+    out: list[ast.AST] = []
+    stack: list[ast.AST] = [scope]
+    while stack:
+        n = stack.pop()
+        out.append(n)
+        stack.extend(c for c in ast.iter_child_nodes(n) if not isinstance(c, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
+    return out

+def _touches(node: ast.AST, tainted: set[str], attrs: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """Does this expression hold settings text? A tainted name, `.environ`/`getenv`, an attribute that was assigned
+    settings text somewhere in the file (`self.raw`), a call of a loader, or a subscript / `.get` with a literal key
+    that looks like a setting name (`cfg["DESK_PORT"]`), whatever the mapping is called."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id in SANITIZERS:
+        return False  # a checked number is not environment text any more
+    for m in ast.walk(node):
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Name) and m.id in tainted:
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Attribute) and (m.attr in ("environ", "getenv", "environb") or m.attr in attrs):
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Call):
+            name = m.func.id if isinstance(m.func, ast.Name) else getattr(m.func, "attr", "")
+            if name in LOADERS:
+                return True
+            if name == "get" and m.args and isinstance(m.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(m.args[0].value, str):
+                if ENV_KEY.fullmatch(m.args[0].value):
+                    return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) and isinstance(m.slice, ast.Constant) and isinstance(m.slice.value, str):
+            if ENV_KEY.fullmatch(m.slice.value):
+                return True
+    return False
+
+
+def _bound(target: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The names and attributes an assignment target binds (a store into `x[k]` binds neither)."""
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Name | ast.Attribute):
+        return [target]
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Tuple | ast.List):
+        return [b for el in target.elts for b in _bound(el)]
+    if isinstance(target, ast.Starred):
+        return _bound(target.value)
+    return []
+
+
+def _analyse(tree: ast.AST) -> tuple[dict[int, set[str]], set[str]]:
+    """Names (per scope) and attributes that hold settings text. Module-level taint is visible in every function; an
+    attribute assigned settings text anywhere in the file (`self.raw = ...`) is tainted wherever it is read."""
+    imported: set[str] = set()
+    for n in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module == "os":
+            imported.update(a.asname or a.name for a in n.names if a.name in ("environ", "getenv", "environb"))
+    scopes = _scopes(tree)
+    by_scope: dict[int, set[str]] = {id(s): set(ENV_NAMES) | imported for s in scopes}
+    attrs: set[str] = set()
+    for s in scopes:
+        if isinstance(s, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
+            for arg in (*s.args.posonlyargs, *s.args.args, *s.args.kwonlyargs):
+                if arg.annotation is not None and ast.unparse(arg.annotation).startswith(
+                    ("Mapping[str, str]", "dict[str, str]")
+                ):
+                    by_scope[id(s)].add(arg.arg)  # def f(e: Mapping[str, str]): e is a settings mapping
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for s in scopes:
+            cur = by_scope[id(s)]
+            if s is not tree:
+                cur |= by_scope[id(tree)]  # module-level taint reaches the functions
+            for n in _walk_scope(s):
+                targets: list[ast.expr] = []
+                value: ast.AST | None = None
+                if isinstance(n, ast.Assign):
+                    targets, value = list(n.targets), n.value
+                elif isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign) and n.value is not None:
+                    targets, value = [n.target], n.value
+                elif isinstance(n, ast.NamedExpr | ast.AugAssign):
+                    targets, value = [n.target], n.value
+                elif isinstance(n, ast.For | ast.comprehension):
+                    targets, value = [n.target], n.iter
+                if value is None or not _touches(value, cur, attrs):
+                    continue
+                for tgt in targets:
+                    for node in _bound(tgt):
+                        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id not in cur:
+                            cur.add(node.id)
+                            changed = True
+                        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr not in attrs:
+                            attrs.add(node.attr)
+                            changed = True
+    return by_scope, attrs
+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the scan: no bare number cast on environment text
+ENV_NAMES = {
+    "env",
+    "environ",
+    "config_env",
+    "os_environ",
+}  # plus any parameter typed Mapping[str, str] or dict[str, str]
+CASTS = {"int", "float", "Decimal"}
+SANITIZERS = {
+    "env_number",
+    "number",
+    "positive_seconds",
+}  # these return a checked number: not environment text any more
+LOADERS = {"load_env", "getenv"}  # calls whose result is settings text
+ENV_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*_[A-Z0-9_]+")  # a literal key such as "DESK_PORT" marks a settings mapping
+SCAN_FOLDERS = ("src", "scripts", "demo_only", "load_tools", "tools")

+def _direct_only(source: str) -> list[int]:
+    """A direct-only scan (the contrast for the full one): a cast whose own argument
+    mentions an env name, a Subscript/Call on one, or `.environ` / `getenv`."""
+    hits = []
+    for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(source)):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id in CASTS and n.args:
+            for m in ast.walk(n.args[0]):
+                if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript | ast.Call):
+                    base = m.value if isinstance(m, ast.Subscript) else getattr(m.func, "value", None)
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Name) and base.id in ENV_NAMES:
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+                    if isinstance(base, ast.Attribute) and base.attr == "environ":
+                        hits.append(n.lineno)
+                        break
+    return hits
+
+
+def _is_cast_expr(node: ast.AST, aliases: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """int, float, Decimal, decimal.Decimal, builtins.int, an alias of one, or functools.partial(<one of these>)."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
+        return node.id in CASTS or node.id in aliases
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
+        return node.attr in CASTS
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
+        fn = node.func
+        is_partial = (isinstance(fn, ast.Name) and fn.id == "partial") or (
+            isinstance(fn, ast.Attribute) and fn.attr == "partial"
+        )
+        return is_partial and bool(node.args) and _is_cast_expr(node.args[0], aliases)
+    return False
+
+
+def _cast_aliases(tree: ast.AST) -> set[str]:
+    """Names that stand for a number cast: `_i = int`, `conv = functools.partial(int)`, `from decimal import Decimal
+    as D`, `from builtins import int as I`."""
+    aliases: set[str] = set()
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for n in ast.walk(tree):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module in ("decimal", "builtins"):
+                for a in n.names:
+                    if a.name in CASTS and (a.asname or a.name) not in aliases and a.asname:
+                        aliases.add(a.asname)
+                        changed = True
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and _is_cast_expr(n.value, aliases):
+                for tgt in n.targets:
+                    if isinstance(tgt, ast.Name) and tgt.id not in aliases:
+                        aliases.add(tgt.id)
+                        changed = True
+    return aliases
+
+
+def _scopes(tree: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """The module and every function."""
+    return [tree, *[n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)]]
+
+
+def _walk_scope(scope: ast.AST) -> list[ast.AST]:
+    """Every node of a scope; the module scope leaves out the function bodies (they are scopes of their own)."""
+    if not isinstance(scope, ast.Module):
+        return list(ast.walk(scope))
+    out: list[ast.AST] = []
+    stack: list[ast.AST] = [scope]
+    while stack:
+        n = stack.pop()
+        out.append(n)
+        stack.extend(c for c in ast.iter_child_nodes(n) if not isinstance(c, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
+    return out
+
+
+def _touches(node: ast.AST, tainted: set[str], attrs: set[str]) -> bool:
+    """Does this expression hold settings text? A tainted name, `.environ`/`getenv`, an attribute that was assigned
+    settings text somewhere in the file (`self.raw`), a call of a loader, or a subscript / `.get` with a literal key
+    that looks like a setting name (`cfg["DESK_PORT"]`), whatever the mapping is called."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id in SANITIZERS:
+        return False  # a checked number is not environment text any more
+    for m in ast.walk(node):
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Name) and m.id in tainted:
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Attribute) and (m.attr in ("environ", "getenv", "environb") or m.attr in attrs):
+            return True
+        if isinstance(m, ast.Call):
+            name = m.func.id if isinstance(m.func, ast.Name) else getattr(m.func, "attr", "")
+            if name in LOADERS:
+                return True
+            if name == "get" and m.args and isinstance(m.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(m.args[0].value, str):
